"In other words, players with normal visa time aren’t necessarily innocent, it might just be that their game hasn’t been selected by the Gallery yet. But players whose visa time clearly exceeds what could normally be obtained in games must be imitators.
"We just need to establish a motion requiring everyone to regularly disclose their remaining visa time, and we can naturally spot anomalies.
"Additionally, we can establish another motion to directly execute imitators through majority vote.
"Today’s broadcast already hinted that players can kill imitators in games and obtain all their visa time. So if we kill an imitator in the community, wouldn’t we also be able to split his visa time?
"Whether for safety or profit, the imitator in our community must die.
"Such a simple method, don’t tell me none of you five thought of it."
Li Renshu nodded, "We naturally thought of it, and more than one person did.
"I even had private discussions with others about this issue.
"But our final conclusion was that not only should such motions not be proposed, they shouldn’t even be discussed in public settings.
"I even had an argument with Officer Cao about this."
Wang Yongxin was stunned. He was very confused, "Why? Do you think the community wouldn’t pass motions like ’voting to execute players’?
"But we’d only know after submitting it and having it rejected."
Li Renshu shook her head slightly, with some helplessness in her tone.
"Brother Wang, managing a company might allow for such thinking. As the boss, you can fire whoever you want, but managing a community doesn’t work that way.
"You can’t investigate everything, right? What if we actually find something?"
Wang Yongxin frowned even more, "What do you mean? Do you already know the imitator’s identity, and he’s someone very important?"
Li Renshu waved her hand, "Of course not. This might be difficult for you to understand, so let me explain slowly.
"First, do you think ’there is an imitator in the community’ is an unchangeable fundamental rule of the New World?
"In other words, if we kill an imitator, is it possible for the Gallery to continue assigning us a new imitator?
"For example, sneaking one in during recruitment, or directly notifying someone on their private computer who wasn’t originally an imitator to become one?"
Wang Yongxin was stunned. He lowered his head in thought for a moment, then nodded.
"What you’re saying makes sense.
"It would most likely happen, no, it would definitely happen 100%."
Everyone had lived in the New World for some time and had gained a fairly deep understanding of the rules here.
The New World was not a utopia, this was already everyone’s consensus.
Since the Gallery believed it necessary to regularly conduct life-and-death games to clean up the useless and the guilty, would the Gallery allow players to kill all the imitators?
Obviously not, as long as the Gallery wanted, if one batch of imitators died, they could immediately select another batch.
As long as players still existed, imitators would always exist because imitators were selected from among the players.
The idea of rooting out and killing all imitators to create an absolutely safe zone was essentially still stuck in the mindset that "the New World could become a utopia."
Li Renshu continued, "So I believe ’confirming the imitator’s identity’ is fine, but ’killing the imitator’ must be done carefully.
"Imitators are also human, some smart, some stupid, some kind, some evil.
"Only those utterly evil imitators who only think about massacring innocents are targets we must kill.
"But if it’s a relatively kind, orderly imitator, even if he’s also killing through life-and-death games, as long as this destruction is within controllable limits, we can’t rashly kill him.
"Because after killing him, what if an even more cunning and evil one comes? Wouldn’t that be more troublesome?
"For relatively kind, orderly imitators, or some simple-minded, easily controlled imitators, our optimal choice is actually to try cooperating with them, let them occupy the imitator position, and prevent the Gallery from inserting more dangerous imitators.
"If possible, we might even extract key information about the next game from them in advance, which could greatly improve our survival rate."
After considering for a moment, Wang Yongxin nodded slightly, "You’re right.
"But since you also agree we should confirm the imitator’s identity as soon as possible, my earlier method is still feasible, right?
"Have everyone disclose their remaining visa time, find suspicious individuals. Then we can negotiate with him, establish a mutually beneficial cooperation model. If he refuses to cooperate, then we consider killing him.
"Either way, the initiative is on our side."
Li Renshu looked at him, "Brother Wang, think about it again.
"Just put yourself in the imitator’s shoes and consider that scenario, and you’ll understand."
This time, Wang Yongxin thought for quite a while.
Finally, he silently sighed, "Alright, from the results perspective, this method is indeed not very controllable."

chapters.title: Chapter 93: Priority of Proposals
chapters.content:
So far, everyone has not lived together in the community long enough, and their understanding of each other is not sufficient enough.
Apart from people with relatively simple thinking like Ding Wenqiang and Su Xiucen, everyone else more or less still wears masks.
On the surface they maintain harmony, and some even appear foolish, but this doesn’t mean that’s truly what they think in their hearts.
Since God’s Imitators can gain the Gallery’s approval and toy with human nature through games, they must also be people who are extremely skilled at hiding their own malice.
If everyone is forced to disclose their visa time and they really do root out a God’s Imitator, that God’s Imitator couldn’t be stupid enough to oppose everyone.
Even if what he’s thinking in his heart is to kill everyone, he would definitely pretend to comply while secretly opposing, putting on an act of cooperation.
This would actually be an even worse situation.
Because when a God’s Imitator doesn’t feel he’s in danger, he might not be so anxious to kill players to ensure his own safety. Whether in daily life or designing life-and-death games, he would be more likely to reveal his true nature when relaxed.
Conversely, if a God’s Imitator realizes he’s in danger and that people in the community might execute him at any time, then he would try every means to kill key players, create chaos in the community, and hide his personality even more carefully.
It would appear that cooperation has been achieved, but in reality, even deeper hidden dangers would be buried.In such a situation, once the player group in the community becomes suspicious of the God’s Imitator, they would definitely tend to kill him directly.
Then the process of "distinguishing whether a God’s Imitator is good or bad, whether cooperation is possible" would completely fail.
After killing him, the Gallery would insert a new God’s Imitator, and after the new God’s Imitator sees the previous example, he would kill people even more frantically. The community people would vote to kill this God’s Imitator too...
This would become an unsolvable cycle.
Wang Yongxin’s method could indeed possibly find the God’s Imitator in the short term, but this would also mean showing all cards to all players in the community, directly putting the God’s Imitator in the most dangerous situation.
Once this layer of pretense is broken, the conflict between the community players and the God’s Imitator would be instantly intensified, with unpredictable consequences.
Of course, if this God’s Imitator is a weakling who can be manipulated at will, then immediately rooting him out would be harmless but if the gamble is wrong, the cost could also be very high, so caution is necessary.
The optimal plan would definitely be to not make noise first, determine the God’s Imitator’s identity without alarming the other party, establish some mutual trust, and then discuss cooperation.
Unless the other party shows extreme tendencies to "kill most people in the community," only then would Wang Yongxin’s method be needed for emergency handling.
Currently, the player mortality rate in Community 17 is not high.
Li Renshu continued, "So, you should understand now, right?
"Some things, once brought into the open, lose flexibility and space, and are very likely to become uncontrollable.
"That’s why I said we can’t investigate everything. What if we really do discover something?
"Besides this, I believe we cannot propose any ’killing proposals,’ and there’s another very important reason:
"This would greatly destroy everyone’s ’sense of security’ in the community.
"Up to now, the reason everyone can live peacefully in the community and communicate friendly is because everyone considers the community a safe zone.
"Only this way will they frankly express their opinions.
"If we propose a killing proposal to kill God’s Imitators, even if this proposal is very harsh, such as: ’Eleven votes in favor are needed to execute a player,’ it would still bring uncontrollable effects.
"Many people would think, this rule is used to kill God’s Imitators today, but what if tomorrow I’m suspected of being a God’s Imitator? Or, I’m a weak person who’s holding everyone back, everyone dislikes me, would they vote to kill me and then recruit other new players?
"You and I might not worry, but there will definitely be others who worry.
"In that case, the community would no longer be a safe zone. In the community, one would also have to consider survival strategies, everyone would scheme against each other, disguise themselves, and even consider striking first.
"Such tense atmosphere would only continuously intensify. Even if we later cancel this killing rule, this trend would be irreversible.
"Because once a killing rule appears, it means the community has broken through the final bottom line. For most people, if something like this happens once, it will happen a second time.
"Moreover, using ’killing God’s Imitators can earn large amounts of visa time’ to promote killing votes, I also think this is inappropriate.
"Killing God’s Imitators from other communities is of course fine, but in one’s own community, killing through proposal voting might bring very serious problems.
"Once players taste the sweetness of voting to kill people to earn large amounts of visa time, this idea will take root and sprout in their hearts.
"If someday Brother Wang, you earn more time in games than God’s Imitators, wouldn’t eleven people also want to kill you?
"For players who have already tried voting to kill people, as long as you have enough visa time, does it matter whether you’re a God’s Imitator or not?
"Even if the probability of such things happening might not be high, do you dare gamble?"
Wang Yongxin was momentarily speechless.
Li Renshu paused, then continued, "As for why we don’t submit ’efficiency’ proposals, but only focus on ’minimum guarantee’...
"Brother Wang, I understand your thinking. To earn more visa time, efficiency is necessary.
"But from the current situation, earning more visa time is not our first priority.
"The probability of dying in games is much higher than the probability of being expelled due to exhausted visa time.
"Through proposals with clear rewards and punishments, transforming the entire community into a militant community that actively participates in games, even ignoring the elimination of the weak and constantly recruiting the strong, this seems like the optimal strategy for extreme survival.
"But the Gallery doesn’t only have extreme survival type games. There are also some games that require passing through compromise, sacrifice, enduring tests of human nature, or professional knowledge in specific fields.
"Just like what was said during previous recruitment, we must try our best to ensure the community’s diversity, because the more homogeneous we become, the easier it is to fall into the same trap and lead to total annihilation.
"As long as players in the community have diversity, there will definitely be stupid people and weak people.
"I even suspect that some communities might establish extremely protective systems for the weak, such as ’all game earnings are equally distributed to all players.’
"Of course, there might also be communities that actively eliminate the weak and only recruit the strong.
"Whether to protect the weak for diversity’s sake, or become social Darwinist and sacrifice diversity? Each community’s choice is different.
"We currently cannot definitively say which method is better, but if overly extreme plans guess wrong, the consequences will be devastating.
"So, we ultimately still adopted a relatively prudent plan, which is our current system.
"In the future, we will consider proposing some proposals that promote efficiency. But now, it’s obviously not that necessary yet."

chapters.title: Chapter 94: Evenly Distributed Time
chapters.content:
Wang Yongxin leaned back in his chair, once again falling into deep thought.
After a long while, he nodded, "Alright, although I don’t completely agree with your viewpoint, from the current situation, what you’re saying is indeed very persuasive.
"Thank you for giving me these explanations.
"Did you think of all this by yourself?"
Li Renshu shook her head, "Of course not, I’m not that smart.
"But I believe that as long as we listen to more opinions, we can always find smarter solutions."
Wang Yongxin stood up from his seat, preparing to leave the room.
"Although our two philosophies might have differences, I also have to admit... you do seem much more reliable than Fu Chen.
"I temporarily acknowledge your community planning approach, but I’ll still continue using my own methods to find the God’s Imitator."
Li Renshu nodded, "You’re not the only one making such attempts."...
After chatting with Wang Yongxin, Li Renshu returned to the main hall to continue reading.
She didn’t know how long she had been reading when she started feeling drowsy, then suddenly heard Fu Chen’s surprised voice.
"You’re back!
"All four of you! All safe! That’s wonderful!"
Li Renshu hurriedly put down her book and looked toward the main hall, only then discovering that the four people who had entered the ’Blind Date Game’ had safely returned to the hall, with no signs of injury whatsoever.
"That’s wonderful."
Li Renshu was also very happy. She was especially worried about Zheng Jie, after all, this young doctor had not participated in any life-and-death games yet, and also seemed somewhat too naive, not cunning enough.
If something went wrong and he died in a game right after arriving at the community, that would be troublesome.
She didn’t know whether the community would supplement new people again in the short term, or whether they could find such suitable candidates.
The big screen also began broadcasting the final results of this game.
[Now announcing Community 17’s final visa time acquisition in the ’Blind Date Game’.]
[Number 9 Xu Tong: 34110]
[Number 10 Zheng Jie: 52792]
[Number 11 Yang Yuting: 24304]
[Number 12 Lin Sizhi: 11122]
[According to community rules, when players obtain visa time greater than 20,000 minutes, 5% will be contributed to the community security fund. The remaining visa time will be credited to each player’s visa.]
Seeing the numbers on the big screen, Li Renshu was stunned for a moment, "Your visa time, why does it have both zeros and non-zeros?
"And both male players’ last digits are 2?"
This was a rather strange phenomenon, because previously, whether in ’Blood Poker’ or ’King’s Judgment,’ everyone’s obtained visa time was in whole hundreds.
Even if situations arose in games where visa time needed to be spent, generally the remainder wouldn’t be calculated to the last digit.
Yang Yuting had still not quite recovered from the shock within the game.
She organized her thoughts a bit and explained, "Because Lawyer Lin killed a God’s Imitator in the game.
"According to the rules, the God’s Imitator’s visa time should have been evenly distributed among the 31 surviving players, which is why there’s a remainder."
Wang Yongxin, who had originally been drinking coffee by the floor-to-ceiling window nearby, almost spat out with a "puff" sound, "What did you say? You killed a God’s Imitator in the game?
"I was just making casual conversation before, did you really find one?"
Other people still in the hall also gathered around. Obviously, everyone wasn’t very interested in exactly how much visa time was earned, but everyone was curious about exactly how the God’s Imitator died.
Even Officer Cao, who was smoking outside, immediately ran over after learning about this matter.
...
On the second floor, Jiang He gently knocked on the door, "Aunt Su, Lawyer Lin and the others killed a God’s Imitator in the game. We’re not sure yet if it’s the one who designed the ’King Judgement’ game.
"We’re preparing to discuss this. Would you like to listen in?"
After a moment, the door opened.
Su Xiucen shook her head, "Thank you for coming to tell me specifically. I’ve been a bit tired these past two days, so I won’t go.
"The computer in the room will also notify about proposals or game invitations, so you don’t need to make a trip every time. Thank you."
Jiang He nodded, "Alright, then Aunt Su, rest well. Call me anytime if you need anything."
...
Not long after, eleven people except Su Xiucen sat around the long table, beginning the review of this game.
Unlike the heavy atmosphere when the ’King Judgement’ ended, this time’s atmosphere seemed cheerful and enthusiastic.
Everyone couldn’t wait to know what the game process was actually like.
The big screen had already pulled up the game rules for the ’Blind Date Game.’
Wang Yongxin asked, "Do you think it’s necessary to purchase the detailed process of this game? I can pay the visa time myself."
Li Renshu shook her head, "Now we have the community security fund. Even if we want to exchange, it should be everyone voting to decide to use the community security fund for the exchange. There’s no need to pay out of pocket.
"But I lean toward not exchanging first. Let the participants do a review first.
"For games with 40 players participating, the detailed process data volume must be very large. If we want to exchange everything, the price will very likely be astronomical."
Wang Yongxin stood up and looked toward the big screen, "Let’s ask about the price first.
"I want to check all player information and result reports for the ’Blind Date Game.’"
[Exchange price for individual player information and result report for ’Blind Date Game’: 72 hours of visa time.]
[Exchange price for all player information and result reports for ’Blind Date Game’: 2880 hours of visa time.]
Wang Yongxin sat back down, "Never mind."
Li Renshu lowered her head, having some difficulty suppressing the smile at the corners of her mouth but she quickly resumed her calm expression and looked at the four people who participated in the game, "Who among you will do a simple review?"
Obviously, regarding purchasing in-game player information and result reports, different games had different prices.
The content of ’Redemption Roulette’ was very simple, and the steps weren’t complex either, so it only required 24 hours of visa time to purchase but ’Blind Date Game’ was much more complex, so the price tripled, becoming 72 hours.
Wanting to buy data for all 40 players became the astronomical figure of 2880 hours, which was enough to bankrupt even players like Wang Yongxin who had relatively more visa time.
Therefore, the optimal choice was still to have the participants narrate first.
If there really were unanswerable difficult problems and doubts, then use visa time to exchange for specific player information.
Xu Tong looked at Zheng Jie, "I think, let Dr. Zheng speak? I feel his game process was the most dramatic.
"Midway I seemed to see you sending a help message to Lawyer Lin, but I don’t know if your problem was solved in the end."
Zheng Jie was somewhat surprised, "Huh? Shouldn’t Lawyer Lin be the one to speak?"
Li Renshu smiled, "If Lawyer Lin speaks, it might cause us to incorrectly estimate the difficulty of this game. Besides, if you speak, we can better analyze your game strategy, find shortcomings from it, and give guidance."
Zheng Jie thought about it, "That seems right too. I do need more guidance. In this game, I really almost died in there.
"It was roughly like this. The first time I entered the meeting room, I encountered Lu Xinyi from Community 3..."
...
The entire game process of more than six hours, Zheng Jie narrated while recalling. By the time he finished speaking, his mouth was dry.
During this time, there were inevitably many parts with errors or omissions, but for those particularly important pieces of information, Lin Sizhi, Yang Yuting, and Xu Tong would make corrections or additions.
Every time he talked about being deceived or doing something stupid, everyone present would sigh, shake their heads, or want to impatiently give advice.
Fu Chen listened with some anxiety, while Wang Yongxin and Cai Zhiyuan frequently held their foreheads, finding it somewhat difficult to comment.
Game reviews within the community had never had such a lively scene before.
After all, those who previously led game reviews were basically smart people like Officer Cao, Wang Yongxin, or Cai Zhiyuan. Even if there were disagreements, there wouldn’t be particularly many clear opposing opinions but many of Zheng Jie’s pig-headed operations indeed made people’s blood pressure rise, and their desire to guide and criticize reached unprecedented heights.
However, this did quickly close the distance between Zheng Jie and everyone in the community.

chapters.title: Chapter 95: Lu Xinyi’s Dual Strategy
chapters.content:
After that, Yang Yuting also stood from the female player’s perspective and briefly described her own game process, as well as the so-called "optimal strategy" that Lu Xinyi told her.
Her ridiculous achievement of easily obtaining 3 likes in the first hour without doing anything left Zheng Jie stunned.
Lin Sizhi also introduced his strategy of spending money to buy likes, and briefly explained why multiple small denomination vouchers would be a better choice than one large denomination voucher.
Zheng Jie suddenly understood, "No wonder Lawyer Lin, you got so many likes in the first 4 hours, and when you left the game you didn’t bring out much visa time. So you spent it in advance!
"I just feel that spending money like this is somewhat wasteful."
Cai Zhiyuan shook his head, "It’s not wasteful at all. In fact, this could be said to be the optimal strategy for male players in the early stage.
"Ensuring your own survival in the game is more important than earning visa time.
"Of course, most players couldn’t prophetically think that killing rules would be updated later, but since this game would ultimately give visa time to male players indiscriminately, and the game’s early stage revolved around ‘Likes’ as the core mechanism, then using visa time to exchange for likes would definitely be the most stable strategy.
"Zhong Yuanyuan’s original intention was to use 30,000 visa time to create imbalance between male and female players and intensify conflicts.
"But male players could also turn around and use this point to their advantage, using long-term benefits to reach stable cooperation strategies with female players."This kind of interest-based cooperation is much more stable than cooperation based on morals or trust.
"In this game, finding trustworthy, stable meeting partners basically puts you in an invincible position.
"Giving female players some concessions doesn’t matter. After all, the final 30,000 minutes of income is real. Even if only 1 minute remains, it’s still profit. The key is whether the concessions can be exchanged for sufficient returns."
Xu Tong was puzzled, "But this method can only be used by male players, right?"
Cai Zhiyuan thought seriously for a moment, then shook his head, "No, female players can also use it, just with different details.
"What do you think, how did Lu Xinyi get that 100% like rate? All through deception? I don’t think so."
Everyone looked at Zheng Jie, then nodded one after another.
Obviously, the kind of deception Lu Xinyi displayed at the beginning could only fool newcomers like Zheng Jie, but wouldn’t work on smarter veterans.
Cai Zhiyuan continued, "What Lu Xinyi said to Yang Yuting, that so-called ’optimal strategy,’ I think at least half of it was lies. You didn’t really believe it, did you?
"She was just fooling other female players. She most likely wouldn’t do that herself.
"When most female players are deceiving for visa time, someone like Lu Xinyi would most likely do the opposite.
"For example, she could completely choose ’Split’ or even ‘I’ll Pay’ after meeting with male players.
"Then propose that she always pays the room fee, in exchange for male players stably matching with her and stably giving her likes.
"What male players need 1000 minutes of visa time to achieve, female players can achieve with just 200 minutes of room fees."
Yang Yuting suddenly understood, "I see, that’s where the trap is!
"She lowered the moral standards of all female players, but lifted herself to moral high ground!
"Just by actively paying room fees, clearly doing the same thing as male players, but it’s enough to make male players grateful.
"It’s all strategy!"
Zheng Jie was somewhat confused, "Huh? So that means Lu Xinyi didn’t scam money?"
Cai Zhiyuan shook his head, "Not necessarily. Someone like her couldn’t possibly not scam money, just that her deception methods wouldn’t be so crude.
"She could completely use both strategies together: on one hand, use active payment and exchanging likes to find stable partners, securing a safety net for herself; on the other hand, occasionally match with some new players to scam money.
"Using different strategies for different players, maximizing benefits.
"In the first 4 hours, getting both likes and money.
"Of course, the prerequisite for doing this is being quite accurate at reading people."
Zheng Jie listened with his mouth agape, "...Someone like her in this game is like a fish in water, in an invincible position!
"Wait, Lawyer Lin, didn’t you encounter Lu Xinyi?
"I was wondering what it would be like if you two met in the meeting room..."
Wang Yongxin was somewhat helpless, "What do you think?
"Both of them established fixed partners very early. Meeting each other would be a low-probability event, right?"
Lin Sizhi nodded, "Yes, I confirmed three stable like-buying candidates very early, so I didn’t need to match with others anymore.
"Meeting Lu Xinyi would require using my brain, which isn’t necessary.
"I still prefer dealing with players with simpler minds."
Li Renshu thoughtfully summarized, "So, analyzing from a god’s perspective, the ’Blind Date Game’ indeed simulated blind date mechanisms, but actually it was an out-and-out killing game, full of malice.
"The God’s Imitator not only hid rules and incited hatred between players to make them kill each other, but also very maliciously formed illegal teams in the game. This was simply a planned massacre.
"Before entering the game, the Gallery said this game’s type was ’screening.’ I don’t quite understand what exactly was screened?"
Yang Yuting thought seriously, "Perhaps precisely because it didn’t have a good ’screening’ effect, the Gallery’s evaluation of it wasn’t high?"
Jiang He was very puzzled, "But similar games should be designed by many God’s Imitators together, right? Shouldn’t the Gallery select an optimal solution?"
Li Renshu shook her head, "I don’t know.
"We currently know nothing about the Gallery’s standards for selecting games, nor do we understand the specific process of the Gallery assigning tasks to God’s Imitators.
"Let’s not speculate blindly. Overthinking might mislead ourselves instead."
Wang Yongxin said calmly, "I think, don’t understand the word ’screening’ so narrowly.
"Just like the Gallery’s definition of ’sinners’ or ’judgment,’ these are also broad concepts. People who haven’t violated laws are also pulled into judgment games.
"Screening can also be indiscriminate random screening.
"Like when big companies interview, if there are too many resumes, they might even randomly throw away some resumes. Euphemistically called, ’luck is also part of ability.’
"Like a natural disaster in nature causing a species to go extinct, this is also a kind of screening.
"The Gallery’s so-called ’screening games’ aim to eliminate some people, but the specific elimination criteria within can be very dynamic, even nonsensical.
"Don’t develop unnecessary misunderstandings about the Gallery because of previous S-rated games, thinking the Gallery will always maintain fairness and justice.
"How could that be possible?
"For the Gallery, it’s certainly good when God’s Imitators create S-rated games targeting human nature, but God’s Imitators creating B or even C-rated garbage games isn’t necessarily completely unusable either.
"The Gallery’s attitude toward God’s Imitators can be said to be extremely tolerant, even indulgent.
"If players die out, they can recruit more. If God’s Imitators die out, they can select more. For the Gallery, even if individual games have extremely unfair situations, it doesn’t matter at all, just like natural disasters in the real world. Who’s going to reason with you?
"If you encounter it, just consider yourself unlucky. Who can you blame for bad luck?
"True strong people, no matter how cruel the environment or how unfair the rules, must adapt. Survival of the fittest.
"For the Gallery, as long as there are enough players, as long as there are enough God’s Imitators, even if the rules aren’t that fair, as long as the general direction doesn’t deviate too much, the final cultivated poison will be excellent enough.
"So I think this ’screening game’ can be seen as an unfair, multi-standard elimination, or as some kind of attempt by the Gallery.
"As I said before, don’t think about whether it’s fair or not. Think about the optimal strategy for survival."

chapters.title: Chapter 96: The Principle of Fortunate Avoidance
chapters.content:
Li Renshu looked at Wang Yongxin and nodded.
Obviously, their previous conversation, especially the discussion about the Gallery’s attitude toward God’s Imitators and players, had given Wang Yongxin some inspiration.
Fu Chen looked at the game rules and said somewhat puzzledly, "I have another question.
"Couldn’t the male players unite from the beginning and use ‘Dislikes’ to threaten the female players in return?
"Everyone clearly only had one like and one dislike per hour. Before the killing rules were clear, the deterrent power of dislikes was the same.
"But after four hours, it became females having more likes and males having more dislikes, with male players making comprehensive concessions."
Wang Yongxin explained, "This is where the game design is ingenious, or rather, full of malice.
"The designer forcibly cut off all connections between players. Communities and same-gender groups couldn’t discuss strategies, only communicating through broadcast data.
"The reason male players couldn’t unite as you suggested is because of a very important principle: ’The Principle of Fortunate Avoidance.’
"For example, in real life you’re someone who lives comfortably without worries about food and clothing. One day on the street you accidentally bump into a furious drunk, it might be him who hit you, but the optimal choice at that moment is for you to actively apologize."This game issued all male players a blank check for 30,000, actually making male players the relative ’fortunate ones’ in the game, so they would spontaneously tend toward active avoidance.
"Combined with the discipline of original social rules, the natural alliance formed by female players due to their ’victim status’ (random deduction of visa time), the inability to communicate with each other within the game, and other factors, the strategy you’re thinking of would be almost impossible to implement.
"Because if you don’t give, plenty of others will. As long as some male players make concessions out of the ’Principle of Fortunate Avoidance,’ then your threat to have females give dislikes becomes meaningless.
"Just like in reality, males are also generally considered the party that benefits more from marriage. Although I don’t agree with this view, it can explain certain phenomena.
"Of course, getting more dislikes and having advantages in the latter four hours is another matter entirely."
Jiang He added, "And doing that would really make it easy for Lawyer Lin to mistakenly kill you as a God’s Imitator, right?"
Everyone laughed. Although this game was indeed very dangerous, the joy of returning safely made it seem even sweeter.
Li Renshu looked at the visa time income she had recorded earlier and nodded thoughtfully, "So, in the end it was 31 players evenly splitting all of that God’s Imitator’s time.
"No wonder your visa times all have remainders.
"But... exactly how much visa time was it?"
Yang Yuting quickly calculated with paper and pen, "I had no additional expenses or income throughout this game, only the parts randomly deducted by the game mechanism.
"3 minutes deducted per hour, so 6 hours should be 18 minutes total deducted, so one share of time should be... 24322.
"Multiplied by 31 gives the total time: 753,984 minutes."
Everyone fell into silence, obviously all somewhat shocked by this astronomical figure.
Zheng Jie realized something was wrong, "Wait, you didn’t spend a penny in this game? Never went Split on room fees even once? Didn’t buy food or water either?"
Yang Yuting thought about it, "In my first four meetings I only encountered one female player, Lu Xinyi, and she actively paid the room fee.
"As for the other male players, they not only actively paid room fees but also brought food and water. I had no place to spend money.
"Later I was always matching with trustworthy players, so I never encountered new players requiring Split again."
Zheng Jie was thunderstruck. Obviously the gap between people in this game was bigger than the gap between people and dogs.
Players with a "wealthy beauty" image like Yang Yuting, even without adopting any sophisticated strategies, could easily win just by displaying normal human-level intelligence but thinking that male players ultimately left the game with 30,000, his psychology balanced out again.
Yang Yuting looked again at the total visa time she calculated and sighed, "750,000 visa time is indeed quite a lot, but unfortunately, divided among 31 players doesn’t leave much."
Jiang He sighed, "Are God’s Imitators all so wealthy? It’s an astronomical figure I can’t imagine at all."
Cao Haichuan corrected, "Strictly speaking, this should be the total visa time of all the deceased in the game.
"When the God’s Imitator is alive, this visa time belongs to her, but when she dies, this visa time gets evenly distributed among the surviving players in the game."
Jiang He looked at Yang Yuting again, "So, the 30,000 minutes of visa time from mutual liking at the end is gone?"
Yang Yuting nodded, "Yes, it should be gone, probably because this game didn’t end normally, but was forcibly settled after the God’s Imitator’s death."
Cai Zhiyuan was thoughtful, "That means there would be two different settlement rules.
"If ’game end’ is the settlement condition, then when forcibly ended due to God’s Imitator death, it would still settle normally. For example, ’male players indiscriminately receive 30,000 minutes of visa time.’
"But if it uses ’last meeting’ as the condition, then it couldn’t settle normally."
Jiang He said regretfully, "That’s such a pity!"
Zheng Jie shook his head, "It’s not really a pity, because the rule about ’extra likes and dislikes costing money’ also didn’t settle, otherwise I would have been charged a lot.
"And most importantly, we came out alive.
"In that situation, even one more meeting could have been life-threatening, let alone persisting to the last meeting."
Li Renshu pondered for a moment, "So, now we’ve come to a very crucial question.
"Could Zhong Yuanyuan be the God’s Imitator who designed ’King’s Judgment’?
"Uncle Ding previously participated in ’Blood Poker’ together with Community 1. So we can’t rule out the possibility that players from Community 1 recognized Uncle Ding and targeted him."
Cai Zhiyuan took the paper and pen and quickly calculated.
"We can’t determine it through visa time.
"Too many deaths. Once the data is slightly averaged out, it’s no longer accurate, and we can’t calculate Zhong Yuanyuan’s original time."
Everyone initially tried to estimate exactly how much visa time the God’s Imitator had. If it was more than 250,000, there would be a possibility it was the God’s Imitator from ’King’s Judgment.’
But obviously this method wouldn’t work.
Cao Haichuan spun his lighter in his palm, "I tend to think that Zhong Yuanyuan and the God’s Imitator from ’King’s Judgment’ are not the same person.
"Her killing methods and visa time harvesting methods are somewhat crude.
"The Gallery gave ’Blind Date Game’ a very low rating, while the God’s Imitator who designed ’King’s Judgment’ could get an S rating. No matter how much their level declined, it wouldn’t drop to this extent.
"Even if the goal was simply and brutally harvesting time, it should be done more skillfully."
If they could prove that Zhong Yuanyuan was the God’s Imitator who designed ’King’s Judgment,’ then her death at this moment would give many people present great peace of mind but unfortunately, no matter how they looked at it, it didn’t seem likely.
Wang Yongxin coughed twice, "It doesn’t matter. Even if this was just a not-so-brilliant God’s Imitator, being able to root her out from the game wasn’t easy. This experience is worth summarizing.
"More importantly, this God’s Imitator showed us a kind of completely new possibility we hadn’t considered before.
"God’s Imitators can actually cooperate with players to turn entire communities into scam operations?
"The Gallery would actually allow such blatant rule-breaking."
Everyone fell into silence. Obviously, Wang Yongxin’s question was equally puzzling to others.
Before this, the vast majority of people understood the relationship between God’s Imitators and players as completely antagonistic.
God’s Imitators design games to slaughter players, while players need to survive in games and then find ways to locate and counter-kill God’s Imitators.
Killing the other party would allow them to seize the other party’s visa time.
The community rules also clearly stated this from the beginning.
[Hidden among all players is a special type of dangerous element: ’God’s Imitators.’ They design games for the Gallery and complete judgments of players.]
[When players die in the Gallery, the designer of the corresponding game will obtain all remaining visa time of that player.]
But the specific case of ’Blind Date Game’ clearly demonstrated the possibility of cooperation between God’s Imitators and players.

chapters.title: Chapter 97: The Formation of a Scam Operation
chapters.content:
Yang Yuting also lowered her head in thought, "I also can’t figure out how mutual trust between the God’s Imitator and players in Community 1 was established?"
Li Renshu seemed to have already thought about this problem and explained, "I think there are two possibilities.
"The first possibility is that Zhong Yuanyuan was the passive party.
"As an incompetent God’s Imitator, she didn’t hide herself well, causing her to be exposed early due to various reasons.
"Community 1 failed to quickly decide how to deal with her. Under the collective surveillance of the entire community, the players collectively coerced the God’s Imitator to design and spoil games, turning the community into a scam operation.
"The second possibility is that Zhong Yuanyuan was the active party.
"She first established her core position within the community through some means, and strongly bound at least five very trustworthy core players, ensuring she wouldn’t be threatened by community proposals.
"Then she passed some kind of proposal within the community to evenly distribute visa time, binding everyone with interests.
"Only then did she reveal her cards, using both coercion and inducement to turn Community 1 into a scam operation."
Zheng Jie was thoughtful, "The second possibility seems higher? After all, Zhong Yuanyuan was in the safest position in the game."Cai Zhiyuan shook his head, "We can’t be so certain. This could also be protective behavior willingly provided by other players. After all, finding such an easily controllable God’s Imitator isn’t easy, and they can’t let her die easily in games."
Wang Yongxin stroked his chin, "But regardless of which situation it is, we can confirm one point:
"For a God’s Imitator to cooperate with players and turn a community into a scam operation, the two sides must be one strong and one weak, not equal in strength.
"One strong and one weak, with one side coercing the other, this kind of cooperation is stable."
Some smart people heard his implication: Community 17 didn’t have such conditions.
From the current situation, Community 17’s average intelligence was obviously higher than Community 1’s, and could even be said to be higher than most communities they’d encountered.
While this was certainly good in community confrontations, it also brought a problem:
Community 17’s God’s Imitator would find it very difficult to establish trust with players.
If this God’s Imitator wasn’t very smart, then seeing the community’s high average intelligence, they would very carefully hide their identity and not dare to expose themselves.
If this God’s Imitator was very smart, then they would hide themselves even more perfectly.
And from the current analysis, it was most likely the latter.
In the short term, players didn’t dare to openly search for the God’s Imitator, or couldn’t find them even if they searched. The God’s Imitator also didn’t want to or dare to go on a killing spree against players for various reasons.
Instead, they were deadlocked.
If "finding the God’s Imitator" was a game of Werewolf, then other communities might have reached the finale right after entering the game.
The God’s Imitator would quickly accidentally expose themselves, or actively expose themselves but Community 17 had stubbornly played until now, with no progress visible at all.
Jiang He looked at everyone somewhat puzzledly, "Since such cooperation mechanisms exist, if our community really has a God’s Imitator, they can actively come forward!
"We can also run a scam operation!
"Our community has so many smart people. As long as we get advance knowledge of game rules, wouldn’t we be invincible?"
After these words, the hall fell into an eerie silence.
Li Renshu looked at Fu Chen and smiled, "Fu Chen! You wouldn’t be that God’s Imitator, would you?"
Fu Chen was stunned for a moment, then laughed, "Ah yes yes yes, I am. You all found me out."
Li Renshu pressed further, "Then what’s the next game? Tell us quickly!"
Fu Chen spread his hands, "How would I know! I haven’t even started designing yet!"
Li Renshu said seriously, "Then when can you finish designing!"
Fu Chen was somewhat helpless, "You’re more demanding than the Gallery! Why don’t you be the Gallery instead."
Everyone laughed. Obviously, this was a joke.
A God’s Imitator wouldn’t actively admit their identity.
Wang Yongxin sighed, "Since our community can hardly establish such cooperation mechanisms, wouldn’t we be very passive in future games?
"This time in the ’Blind Date Game,’ Community 1’s scam operation was witnessed by 4 other communities besides us.
"After they return, will they also be inspired and learn Community 1’s methods?
"And Community 1 too, although Zhong Yuanyuan is dead, the Gallery will very likely supplement them with a new God’s Imitator.
"Community 1’s players can completely coerce the new God’s Imitator to continue this model.
"In that case, every time we enter games, we might not only encounter God’s Imitators who know all the rules, but also players who know the rules in advance.
"Then what’s the point of playing these games anymore? Don’t let everyone else have scripts while we don’t."
Jiang He nodded, "Exactly! So which big brother or sister in our community is the God’s Imitator, please come out quickly!
"This is for our common benefit. We must cooperate now!"
Wang Yongxin glanced at Jiang He, wanting to speak but stopping himself.
Jiang He’s behavior was somewhat foolish, because Community 17’s God’s Imitator obviously couldn’t come out. Calling for them was pointless but sometimes, community discussions still needed these relatively foolish statements as catalysts.
Otherwise, if everyone was smart, with a table full of riddle-speakers all staring at each other, how could they play?
Cai Zhiyuan was thoughtful, "The more we talk about this, the more incredible it seems that Lawyer Lin was able to dismantle this scam operation.
"After all, ’God’s Imitators can run scam operations’ was the biggest information gap.
"Without realizing this point, at most you’d lock suspicion onto Gao Jialiang or Fang Wencong.
"Unable to kill Zhong Yuanyuan, the game wouldn’t end, and you might instead put yourself in danger.
"Lawyer Lin, how did you think of it?"
Lin Sizhi looked at Cao Haichuan, "Actually, this was inspiration I received from chatting with Officer Cao before.
"Officer Cao explained many case-solving principles to me in detail. Simply put, the most important point in rooting out God’s Imitators is to deduce their motives through game rules.
"For example, the motive of ’Blind Date Game’ was easy to deduce: the varied killing rules directly wrote ’I want to kill more people to earn visa time’ on their face.
"According to the game mechanism, since they wanted to kill more people, they had to quickly incite hatred and opposition between genders.
"Because if hatred wasn’t enough, it would be hard to form a spiral of mutual harm between male and female players in the latter 4 hours, and not enough people would die.
"So, the God’s Imitator had to incite opposition through broadcasts early, and after the game entered the second phase with updated killing rules, quickly kill to create a terrifying atmosphere.
"To kill quickly, they had to prepare enough dislikes in advance.
"With these thoughts, the probability of finding the God’s Imitator greatly increased. ’Broadcasting early’ and ’abnormal like-dislike ratios’, these two points let me successfully lock onto Community 1.
"I didn’t have 100% certainty, but in that situation, I could only make the greatest effort to try."
Everyone followed his gaze and looked at Cao Haichuan.
Cao Haichuan nodded, "I did explain the approach, but being able to implement this strategy in a high-risk environment where you completely couldn’t communicate with community players and could die at any moment was indeed remarkable."

chapters.title: Chapter 98: The Gallery’s Attitude
chapters.content:
Everyone nodded. Originally they thought finding the God’s Imitator was an incredible feat, but now thinking about it, each step of the reasoning was traceable.
Especially since Officer Cao was a professional criminal investigator, his guidance was also crucial.
Li Renshu nodded in agreement, "Indeed, the God’s Imitator’s purpose often becomes the key to our breakthrough. Things might not be as bad as we think."
Cao Haichuan picked up the conversation, "I also agree with this view. As I guessed before, killing for God’s Imitators isn’t without cost.
"The more purpose-driven a God’s Imitator is, the easier they are to catch in games.
"And if their purpose isn’t strong, or they don’t dare to blatantly exploit backdoors that most people can’t discover in games, then the game’s fairness can still be fundamentally guaranteed."
Fu Chen realized a problem, "Wait, I suddenly realized there’s still one point we’ve never clarified: do God’s Imitators have to enter their own games?
"This point is very important!"
Everyone fell silent. Obviously, this question still had no clear answer.
Li Renshu looked at Lin Sizhi, "Lawyer Lin, what do you think? You should have the most authority on this question."Lin Sizhi spread his hands, "I don’t know.
"The reason I worked toward ’finding the God’s Imitator’ was because the broadcast before the game specifically mentioned the rules about killing God’s Imitators. This rule was very likely the Gallery hinting to us: this game has a chance to kill the God’s Imitator.
"But the Gallery didn’t directly reveal this point after all, so I couldn’t be completely certain either."
Zheng Jie was stunned, "Huh? You weren’t completely certain? Your sense of conviction at the time completely convinced me!"
Lin Sizhi smiled somewhat helplessly, "That was the most likely scenario, and the only way to break the situation. Even if I wasn’t completely certain, I could only choose to say that.
"Otherwise what could I say? Tell everyone ’the God’s Imitator might not be in this game’? Did I work so hard to audition just to spoil the mood?
"I had to appear absolutely certain to convince other players to vote to kill. If I showed even a hint of hesitation, we might not have gathered 20 votes.
"As for what to do if the God’s Imitator wasn’t in the game?
"What else could we do? Everyone would show their abilities and persist until the game ended.
"As for Community 1’s players, if we killed the wrong people, so be it. They incited the most opposition and were all indirect murderers anyway."
Jiang He frowned, "I think God’s Imitators definitely have to enter the game, right?
"If they could choose not to enter games, there might be a very ridiculous way to exploit loopholes!
"The God’s Imitator turns the community into a scam operation, reveals all rules in advance, then only lets other players enter while staying out themselves. Wouldn’t that be invincible?"
Li Renshu nodded, "Mm, that makes sense too.
"The Gallery might allow God’s Imitators to engage in some high-risk, high-reward behaviors, such as playing with open cards in the community. God’s Imitators would also have to bear the risk of being coerced, controlled, or even killed by community players.
"But running scam operations while not participating themselves would be too excessive and would seriously affect the balance between God’s Imitators and players.
"The Gallery shouldn’t completely turn a blind eye."
Fu Chen thought about it, "Perhaps as Lawyer Lin said, the Gallery specifically disclosing rules about killing God’s Imitators before entering the game is some kind of hint.
"But...
"Just this isn’t enough, right? The Gallery can’t broadcast such information every time God’s Imitators enter their own games, can they?"
Wang Yongxin spread his hands, "If the Gallery really doesn’t care, we have no solutions anyway. Players are all meat on the chopping board, just the difference between early and late cutting."
Li Renshu stared at the rules on the big screen and suddenly realized something.
She stood up and came to the big screen, pointing at the five rules in the bottom right corner.
"Perhaps the Gallery has already limited this behavior.
"Don’t you find it strange? Why would these five rules be written here separately? And specifically noted as ’supplementary rules’?"
Lin Sizhi had already noticed these five rules long ago, but since no one mentioned them, he naturally wouldn’t bring them up proactively.
Now Li Renshu finally noticed.
These five rules, the first four were the four rules he had once submitted to Zhong Yuanyuan.
And the fifth rule was:
[5. The God’s Imitator who designed this game will personally enter the game.]
Many people showed expressions of surprise. They indeed hadn’t noticed this point before.
Because the ’Blind Date Game’ had too many rules, the entire big screen was densely packed, making people’s eyes hurt. Everyone only roughly understood through following Zheng Jie’s review.
These five supplementary rules at the end weren’t obvious.
Xu Tong was thoughtful, "These five... might be the God’s Imitator being unsatisfied with their own plan, so they patched it?
"That’s normal, right? After all, when we make plans, we often have omissions that need modification."
Li Renshu shook her head slightly, "But all the games we’ve seen before, all games, have never had similar post-modification situations.
"What the Gallery shows us are complete rules, with items strictly displayed in chronological order in a modular way.
"Even if God’s Imitators want to modify their own rules, they would definitely modify them privately and submit them after everything is fixed, right?
"Supplementary rules should also be inserted into corresponding previous positions. How could they just be randomly appended at the end like this?
"Would you dare present such a formatted plan to your boss or leader? You’d definitely get scolded.
"The Gallery’s review standards should be even stricter."
Wang Yongxin nodded, "That makes sense."
Obviously, as a civil servant, Li Renshu had extraordinary sensitivity to ’format.’
This kind of writing where subsequent rules were just appended at the end was almost like committing a cardinal sin in Li Renshu’s eyes, very conspicuous indeed.
She continued, "I believe these rules were personally added by the Gallery to balance game difficulty.
"Because careful analysis reveals that these rules are indispensable, whether for players’ self-protection or helping players better determine the God’s Imitator’s position."
Wang Yongxin was stunned, "Wait, how can you be certain these were personally added by the Gallery?
"It’s also possible the Gallery rejected the original draft and forced the God’s Imitator to make adjustments and additions, so Zhong Yuanyuan was forced to add these rules to make the game fairer."
Li Renshu pointed to the last rule, "’The God’s Imitator who designed this game will personally enter the game.’
"Besides the Gallery, who has the authority to write this sentence in the rules?
"Zhong Yuanyuan could write it herself, but would she be foolish to that extent? Even if she wanted to enter the game to see the crime scene, there would be no need to specifically write it in the rules, right?"
Zheng Jie suddenly understood, "Oh? I see!
"These rules, at first glance seem favorable to the God’s Imitator, but upon careful consideration, are actually favorable to players.
"Take the third rule for example. When I was ’bluffing’ before, I thought about how the 10-second death waiting time could actually increase gaming space between players.
"But...
"The first two rules don’t seem to have any special effects?
"Take the vouchers for example. If I could return them myself, I would consider buying them. After all, they wouldn’t be stuck in my hands, at most I’d lose 20% in handling fees.
"But since they can’t be returned, I never could make up my mind to purchase them."

chapters.title: Chapter 99: Dynamic Balance
chapters.content:
Cao Haichuan said matter-of-factly, "It’s normal that you find this puzzling.
"It’s precisely because these rules are more deceptive to God’s Imitators that Zhong Yuanyuan misjudged the power gap between herself and the players in the game.
"She thought she was in an invincible position, while the players could only be slaughtered by her at will, but in reality it wasn’t the case."
Wang Yongxin pointed to the first two supplementary rules:
"The first rule, precisely because exchange tickets cannot be returned by oneself and can only be given to other players, allows for establishing long-term cooperation with others.
"If they could be returned by oneself, the other party would worry that such promises would become empty checks, which would actually be detrimental to building mutual trust.
"As for the second rule, I believe that although it intensified the conflicts between male and female players, it also serves a crucial purpose, which is secondary confirmation.
"If we only relied on ’like-to-dislike ratio’ to determine the God’s Imitator, it would still lack some persuasive power.
"Take Gao Jialiang for example, his like-to-dislike ratio was 54%. Does this necessarily mean he was actively seeking dislikes?
"Maybe male players were jealous and gave him dislikes? Or maybe some female players thought he lacked masculine energy?"Just the 54% ratio, although somewhat abnormal, wasn’t enough to convince all players.
"But the Split button data was enough to form a stark contrast, making 54% become indisputably abnormal data.
"Overall, the abnormality in like-dislike data only raises suspicion, but isn’t solid evidence.
"To convince 20 players to vote ’boring’ to help you kill someone, you need another set of data for double confirmation.
"Moreover, the existence of this data can also remind more players to notice abnormalities in the game, alerting them to the fact that ’the God’s Imitator might be deliberately stirring up conflicts in the game.’"
Zheng Jie suddenly understood, "I see... I’ve learned something."
Jiang He thought of another question, "What if Gao Jialiang actively pressed ‘I’ll Pay’ every time? Wouldn’t the data show no abnormality?"
Cai Zhiyuan shook his head, "No, there would still be abnormality.
"A handsome guy like him, pressing ‘I’ll Pay’ every time, then only receiving 54% likes, wouldn’t that be even stranger?
"As long as he wants to actively seek dislikes, this data will always show inconsistencies.
"Conversely, if he wants to make his data appear normal, he can’t get enough dislikes in the first 4 hours, making it impossible to execute subsequent plans.
"This is a dead end, the result is the same regardless of what he chooses."
Jiang He nodded convincingly, "I see! This structure is quite ingenious.
"So... the Gallery personally intervened, embedding rules and hints in the game that are sufficient for players to counter-kill the God’s Imitator?
"And for these unfair games, the Gallery forcibly requires God’s Imitators to enter?
"What exactly is the Gallery? Is it truly an omnipotent god?
"Regardless, as long as the Gallery is willing to personally intervene and fine-tune game rules, then even if God’s Imitators run rigged operations, players won’t be completely at their mercy.
"If God’s Imitators behave even more outrageously, the Gallery will likely continue to increase the intensity of sanctions."
Li Renshu nodded, "Yes, I even believe the Gallery deliberately selected some relatively intelligent players to enter the game.
"According to this game’s selection rules, although it mandates the three players with the least visa time from each community to enter, there are also voluntary registration and Gallery-mandated quotas.
"Cases like Lu Xinyi and Lawyer Lin were voluntary registrations, because from the community’s perspective, strong players must enter the game to lead the team, ensuring the safety of players from the same community while earning more visa time.
"Some very intelligent players who don’t want to participate might also be forcibly pulled in by the Gallery.
"After these intelligent people are threatened in the game, they consistently point their spears at the God’s Imitator of that game.
"In the game, Lawyer Lin wasn’t the only one checking data, many players from other communities were also investigating.
"Although from the results, Lawyer Lin’s behavior seemed like some kind of individual heroism performance, there were still two hours left before the game ended at that time.
"Even without Lawyer Lin, I believe intelligent players would still have locked onto the first community before the game ended and taken action.
"Fang Wencong’s death was very likely proof of other players taking action."
Everyone nodded, each lost in thought, and their originally worried expressions gradually relaxed.
In other words, when a certain God’s Imitator commits obviously transgressive behavior, although the Gallery won’t directly kill them or reject their game, they will likely balance the game difficulty through two methods.
First, the Gallery personally supplements rules, and second, when screening players, they deliberately select strong ones.
Although many doubts still exist, the conclusion that ’the Gallery will dynamically balance gameplay’ still gave everyone considerable peace of mind.
Li Renshu looked at the time, "Alright, this debriefing session ends here.
"It now appears that ’screening-type games’ also have a certain mortality rate, possibly even higher than judgment-type games.
"However, the difference is that screening-type games often don’t target specific players, nor do they necessarily test human nature, but rather include large numbers of players and then eliminate the weak according to rules.
"Our conservative player selection strategy this time was correct. If 8 people had really entered, in situations where they couldn’t help each other at all, more casualties might have occurred.
"The communities that died most in this game were the 9th and 12th communities, precisely because they entered significantly more players than others.
"Due to game mechanics issues, not only was it impossible to execute team strategies, but one player attracting hatred would doom the entire community’s players.
"Next time we encounter this type of screening game, we must still be cautious.
"Alright, everyone must be tired. Let’s end here for today.
"In any case, everyone returned safely, and Doctor Zheng also earned considerable visa time. Today is a day worth celebrating. Everyone go rest well, let’s have a group dinner tonight!"
Xu Tong was very happy, "Great! Group dinner!"
Everyone stood up and left one by one.
...
Evening.
The lobby was brightly lit as everyone spontaneously prepared dinner.
Some discussed what dishes to order at the vending machine, some washed dishes, and some tidied tables.
Li Renshu had just given Xu Tong some menu suggestions when she turned around and happened to see Su Xiucen walking down from the second floor.
"Aunt Su.
"Are you feeling better?"
Su Xiucen smiled, "Much better now. Is there anything I can do? If you liked those home-cooked dishes from before, I can make them again."
Li Renshu supported her arm, "No need, Aunt Su. You’ve worked hard during this period too. We can’t always make you toil during group dinners.
"This time just enjoy the food with us, put all those miscellaneous things aside."
Su Xiucen nodded, "Alright."
Soon, various dishes filled the long table, and everyone took their seats.
As before, they bought some relatively cheap red wine, champagne, and beverages, but everyone took what they wanted according to their own preferences.
Wang Yongxin looked at the champagne in his wine glass and sniffed it at his nose.
"What a pity, this cheap champagne still tastes inferior.
"If there were no rule restrictions, I’d want to pay for a more expensive bottle myself for everyone to try."
Speaking, he looked toward Li Renshu, "When will we add another motion specifically for a ’luxury consumption fund’?
"Everyone voluntarily deposits visa time into it to buy high-end food, clothing, or cosmetics for everyone.
"After all, there are so many expensive things in the vending machine that we haven’t enjoyed yet."

chapters.title: Chapter 100: The Gallery’s Reward
chapters.content:
Li Renshu smiled, "What, is this going to be ’Boss Wang pays for everyone’s consumption’? I’m not used to you being so generous all of a sudden."
Wang Yongxin waved his hand with a smile, "Hey, I’m not a stingy person to begin with, you have a misunderstanding about me.
"In business, in deals, haggling over every penny, that’s for profit.
"In daily life, being generous when treating people to meals, that’s for relationships.
"Each has its place.
"When running a company, although costs that should be saved must definitely be saved, the relationships that should be maintained must definitely be maintained, otherwise who would work for you among those who truly have ability?"
Li Renshu nodded, "Alright, then we’ll wait to benefit from Boss Wang’s generosity in the future."
This was perhaps Wang Yongxin’s attempt to buy people’s hearts with visa time, but in this setting, Li Renshu naturally couldn’t categorically refuse in an overly serious manner.
As for whether to actually propose this motion later, that would naturally require long-term consideration.
Everyone had smiles on their faces, and the atmosphere in the lobby was good.Li Renshu coughed lightly twice, "Today is a special day, so I think we need some sense of ceremony.
"I’d like to take up a little of everyone’s time to say a few brief words.
"Now we’ve understood most of the New World’s rules. In our days living in the New World, we’ve endured the parting of companions and also felt the joy of new members arriving.
"I know that such dramatic changes between great joy and great sorrow aren’t easy for most people.
"Although we haven’t known each other very long in the community, and can only be considered chance acquaintances, we should still cherish every friendship, every bond.
"We should remember those who have passed away, and also learn to adapt to this cruel environment, looking forward with optimistic, positive attitudes.
"This drink is both in memory of Uncle Ding and to welcome Doctor Xiao Zheng.
"Most importantly, no matter what happens, we will always be the best Community 17.
"Come on, everyone raise your glasses."
Everyone picked up their wine or beverages, "Cheers!"
That night, many people chatted in the lobby until very late.
...
At 10 PM, Lin Sizhi returned to his room.
Sure enough, a new game invitation appeared again on his personal computer.
And it was an invitation to a judgment game.
"The King of Hell calls the roll, not giving any time to rest."
Lin Sizhi felt somewhat helpless, but he first looked at the time, which was still quite ample, this game would only start a week later.
[Hello, Lin Sizhi.]
[You have cleared an incompetent God’s Imitator for the New World. The Gallery will remember your contribution.]
[When excellent God’s Imitators prove their value to the Gallery, they will accumulate two advantages:]
[More lenient review standards, and more available scene props.]
[In addition, you will gain basic access to the ’Database,’ which can be consulted through your personal computer.]
"Hmm?"
Lin Sizhi read through this content again.
Clearly, these two advantages were of great significance.
For God’s Imitators to survive in the New World, one thing was likely as important as life itself, that their self-designed games successfully get selected.
If they failed to be selected, then God’s Imitators would be equivalent to good people holding werewolf identity cards, not only having no benefits but also being suspected by other players.
God’s Imitators not recognized by the Gallery might be killed by players, might accidentally die in other God’s Imitators’ life-and-death games, might become puppets of other players, or might be eliminated by the Gallery through various methods.
But if every game could be successfully selected, then the God’s Imitator identity would be all advantages.
Taking a step back, they could leave backdoors in their own games to ensure self-preservation.
Going further, they could set traps to kill people they wanted to kill, or save people they wanted to save through rules.
Going even further, they could slowly change the Gallery’s rules through their own games, thereby influencing the entire New World’s ecosystem.
Even if excellent God’s Imitators became public enemies of the community, they would still have sufficient strategic space for self-preservation.
More available scene props could not only increase players’ immersion but also mix in some hints about game content in the details.
And once such hints worked in coordination with game rules, they could also significantly improve the Gallery’s evaluation of the game.
The lenient review standards went without saying, this meant games with hidden agendas would be more easily selected.
It was like the promotion path for workers in a company.
Newly hired workhorses could only strictly follow leadership requirements to produce proposals, having to guess the leader’s intentions and find ways to work miracles in limited space, showing their ingenuity in some details.
But after successive promotions, having achieved a certain position, they could autonomously design proposals, increasingly not needing to look at others’ faces.
Even reaching a certain level, willfulness and personal gain within unwritten rules would be overlooked with a blind eye.
Eliminating Zhong Yuanyuan, this incompetent God’s Imitator, indeed made Lin Sizhi take certain risks but even if ordinary players in the community had some suspicions, they couldn’t find any reliable evidence, after all the Gallery intentionally provided cover for Lin Sizhi.
Whether it was the hints before entering the game or the fifth supplementary rule additionally added after updating game rules, both would make players mistakenly think the Gallery was personally intervening to dynamically adjust game difficulty.
The existence of this information gap made it very difficult for ordinary players to imagine that this game was actually a confrontation between two God’s Imitators, and might instead reduce suspicion about Lin Sizhi’s God’s Imitator identity.
After all, from other players’ perspectives, if Lin Sizhi himself was a God’s Imitator, he definitely wouldn’t lack visa time, so why would he risk participating in games designed by other God’s Imitators? Was his life too easy and he was looking for thrills?
For God’s Imitators, they would definitely avoid participating in other God’s Imitators’ games if possible. Only for players would participating in any game be about the same.
According to common sense, the more eagerly players participated in Gallery games, the less likely they were to be God’s Imitators because there was absolutely no need to risk their lives for such a disguise.
So Lin Sizhi’s proactive participation this time was a righteous act of ’helping vulnerable players,’ making it easier to solidify his good person identity.
However, one point worth noting was that Lin Sizhi wasn’t certain whether the Gallery would send modification suggestions to other God’s Imitators.
If they sent them to other God’s Imitators, and their modification suggestions weren’t selected, then when they entered the ’Blind Date Game,’ they would definitely realize that some God’s Imitator might have modified this game’s rules, and deduce from the Gallery’s previous rules that another God’s Imitator had also entered the game.
This way, there would also be the possibility of deeply suspecting Lin Sizhi.
But Lin Sizhi ultimately didn’t know whether the Gallery had actually sent modification suggestions to other God’s Imitators, and moreover, even if such God’s Imitators existed, they wouldn’t pose much threat in the short term.
Unless the other party was stupid enough to prefer self-destruction rather than drag Lin Sizhi down with them.
Even if it came to that step, Lin Sizhi wouldn’t be helpless. Although he currently didn’t want to expose his identity, it didn’t mean he couldn’t handle things after his identity was exposed.
As early as when he voluntarily pulled the trigger in ’Redemption Roulette,’ he had already been fully prepared.
Playing with cards face up naturally had its own methods.
From the current gains, taking risks to enter the game and clearing God’s Imitators for the Gallery was worth it.

chapters.title: Chapter 101: Judgment Game Invitation
chapters.content:
"What is the Database?"
Lin Sizhi searched around on his personal computer and soon found a brand new icon that had just appeared: ’Database.’
This was something like an AI Q&A software, with just an input box where you could type questions and it would automatically generate answers.
Lin Sizhi thought for a moment and directly typed, "Give me the list of all God’s Imitators in the Gallery."
Soon, the Database gave a clean and straightforward reply.
[Sorry, this question does not comply with Gallery rules and cannot be answered.]
"Heh, I knew it."
Lin Sizhi thought for a moment and changed the question, "Give me the list of all audience members in ’King’s Judgment.’"
[Sorry, this question does not comply with Gallery rules and cannot be answered.]
"The total number of communities currently in the New World."[Sorry, this question does not comply with Gallery rules and cannot be answered.]
Lin Sizhi was somewhat helpless, "Then what exactly can I check with this basic access?"
He thought for a moment and entered again, "Price of 500g apples."
[In the community, the price of 500g apples is: 15 minutes of visa time.]
[In the real world, the price of 500g apples generally ranges from 4-20 yuan depending on regional, variety, seasonal and other factors.]
Finally, he got a definitive answer.
Lin Sizhi considered for a moment and entered another question, "How many street lamps are there on 1 square kilometer of land?"
[In the community, this question does not comply with Gallery rules and cannot be answered.]
[In the real world, the number of street lamps on 1 square kilometer of land could be 0-1800.]
[Adding filtering conditions can provide more accurate data.]
"Somewhat humorous, do I need to ask you about real world conditions?"
Lin Sizhi’s original intention was to roughly estimate how many communities there were here by asking about the number of street lamps in the New World, but unexpectedly this couldn’t be checked either.
Instead, the data for the real world was very detailed, and if he continued asking, he could further refine these results.
After studying it for a while, Lin Sizhi made a precise definition of it: "Toy."
He closed the Database and continued viewing the Gallery’s notification.
[In seven days, the Gallery will open several different judgment games. You have been assigned six sinners.]
[In your desk drawer, there are criminal files for these six sinners, along with corresponding judgment results.]
[In this game, you may select 2-6 sinners from the six for judgment. At the same time, you may also set additional conditions to select 1 specific player from the sinner’s community to forcibly enter the game.]
[Other unrelated players may voluntarily participate in the game, with specific numbers determined by you.]
[You may freely choose whether to design this game.]
[But remember:]
[No matter how sinners evade, the Gallery’s judgment will eventually come.]
[The Gallery will evaluate all submitted planning documents and adopt the highest-scoring proposal to set up the game venue.]
[Now, the 120-hour countdown begins. Please make your choice.]
"From the description, it seems these six sinners don’t have strong connections."
Lin Sizhi quickly determined this through the different descriptive information from two judgment game invitations.
The previous judgment game invitation made it very clear: the Gallery assigned judgment games by cases, and Lin Sizhi was assigned to ’Case C.’
All five sinners belonged to Case C, so they were forced to participate in the game, while the other 10 players voluntarily participated.
Therefore, smarter God’s Imitators should have realized then that the crimes of those five people were related but this judgment game was different.
Lin Sizhi was assigned six sinners and could select 2-6 of them to participate in the judgment game, which meant their crimes had no strong connections.
They might simply be similar types of crimes grouped into one category.
Lin Sizhi could even easily help some of these criminals escape this judgment: he just needed to select any two criminals for judgment.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs NovᴇlFirenᴇt
The other four criminals wouldn’t need to enter this game at all.
This change in freedom might also be a manifestation of his elevated status in the Gallery.
However, the Gallery also gave a warning: No matter how sinners evade, the Gallery’s judgment will eventually come.
In other words, if Lin Sizhi let a certain sinner go this time, it didn’t mean they were safe.
New judgment games would still come.
Before this sinner actually entered a judgment game and survived, there would always be a sword of Damocles hanging over their head.
Perhaps next time the Gallery would give their file to another God’s Imitator for judgment.
Of course, whether a certain sinner had multiple crimes and would be arranged for multiple judgments was still unknown.
Besides this, the change in selection rules was also noteworthy.
Lin Sizhi could also select anyone from the sinner’s community to forcibly enter the game.
"This way, it’s more concealed for God’s Imitators to kill people.
"But this is mostly a privilege only excellent God’s Imitators have."
Previously, it wasn’t easy for God’s Imitators to kill a specific player.
Because for screening-type games, the target might not register to participate, while for judgment-type games, it depended on whether the Gallery would select the target as a sinner but now, Lin Sizhi could completely design a judgment game, then force a player from the same community as a sinner to enter, burying traps targeting them in the judgment game.
This type of design where "the drinker’s intent lies not in the wine" was now within the allowed range.
"Should I try it?"
Lin Sizhi couldn’t make a decision for now. He planned to first look at the specific list of sinners.
He took out the planning document from the drawer, roughly scanned it, and found it wasn’t much different from previous planning documents, except that the ’Available Props List’ column was much shorter than before but shorter didn’t mean fewer available props. On the contrary, most had become freely designable props, and the quantities had significantly increased.
Two props particularly caught Lin Sizhi’s attention.
[3. Computers with at most 5 system functions: 20 units.]
[5. Virtual outdoor scenes that can simulate real scenarios.]
Besides these, there were many customizable props with high freedom and large quantities.
Lin Sizhi took out the sinner files, first swept his hand across the desktop to spread out the files, roughly looked at these people’s names to see if there were any acquaintances.
This time the files noted which communities the sinners were in, and there was no deliberate concealment of crimes like last time.
This might be because these criminals didn’t belong to the same case, and deliberately concealing crimes would prevent God’s Imitators from determining the judgment game’s content, so all crimes had to be disclosed.
[Community 8, Tian Fan].
[Community 8, Jiao Hongtao].
"Jiao Hongtao? This seems like a player I encountered before in the ’Blind Date Game.’"
[Community 17, Su Xiucen].
Lin Sizhi’s movements stopped for a moment.
Then he took out this file separately and read it carefully.
[Su Xiucen, female, 52 years old.]
[Occupation: Retired worker.]
[To cure her husband’s lung cancer contracted during his time as a miner, despite knowing there was no hope of cure, she still sought medical treatment everywhere and prayed to gods and buddhas. Despite repeated dissuasion, she remained obstinate, ultimately losing both her family and fortune. The donated money became operating funds for fraud groups, causing more innocent people to lose their homes and fortunes.]
[Punishment result: Not yet judged]
Lin Sizhi looked at the content in the file and fell into deep thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 102: Financial Sources Game
chapters.content:
One week later.
Xu Tong had just come down from the second floor, preparing to order breakfast at the vending machine, when she saw new prompts appear on the big screen.
[Good morning, players!]
