"If it were reversed and Li Jiang used mechanism 1, with sufficient stamina he very likely would have tried using it consecutively. In that case, we’d be more likely to discover this mechanism..."
Qin Yao said somewhat surprised, "Put this way, Lawyer Lin’s initial ’kill all’ suggestion really was the simplest solution to this game?
"Three questions total, two chances to ask for help. Even answering only 2 correctly, if all criminals were killed, that’s a total of 300,000 childbirth fund.
"Even with only Li Jiang alone, you could choose to have him use the 15,000 tier when using mechanism 1.
"Then you three female players could share mechanism 2, three times each, with plenty of surplus remaining.
"If all three questions could be answered correctly, that goes without saying, you could even have several completely harmless chances."
Li Renshu nodded, "Yes, actually we audience members realized this during the game.
"Kill all is the simplest and most direct clearance method.
"Besides this, you could also choose to kill the 2 people in the first prisoner room, choose disciplinary action for the next 4, or kill the first 4 and choose not guilty for the last two.
"Save all isn’t very reliable, because both ’not guilty’ and ’disciplinary action’ require spending childbirth fund. If only 2 questions are answered correctly, the margin for error would be much lower than kill all."
Yang Yuting felt very defeated, "We didn’t think at all that ’kill all’ was the suggestion Lawyer Lin gave! This is completely unlike your character!"
Lin Sizhi spread his hands, "I emphasize again, this suggestion was just the most feasible clearance suggestion I gave from the audience’s perspective. It doesn’t represent my professional ethics or my personal true views.
"If I were playing this game myself, I would definitely use other methods.
"Don’t let my reputation suffer because of a game suggestion."
Yang Yuting asked again, "But how did Lawyer Lin think of this right when entering the game?"
Lin Sizhi explained, "Mainly because of the information gap.
"The audience knew information about ’consistency voting,’ so they could infer the God’s Imitator’s game design thinking based on this hidden rule.
"The childbirth torture devices had three different tiers, meaning there exists a clearance method of ’fewer people but reducing mechanism difficulty through additional childbirth fund.’
"’Kill all’ wouldn’t affect consistency voting and could obtain additional childbirth fund. It’s most likely a stable clearance route.
"Of course, the God’s Imitator who designed this game also limited this strategy: they required judgment panel members to personally take action and complete the death penalty judgment with a dagger."
Yang Yuting obviously hadn’t figured out this issue either, "Yes, requiring us to personally kill people, what kind of twisted taste is this?
"Wouldn’t it be simpler to have mechanisms kill them, or instant death?"
Lin Sizhi explained, "This counts as a simple test, and would also affect ’consistency voting’ to some degree.
"Making a death penalty judgment is a relatively serious matter.
"Wrongful executions certainly can’t be completely avoided, but at least, the person making a death penalty judgment for the first time should look the criminal in the eyes and take responsibility for their judgment.
"In some Western literary works, lords personally execute death penalties and always look the condemned in the eyes. This rule becomes a tradition passed down through generations in the lord’s family.
"At least for the first execution, carrying it out personally ensures one retains a baseline reverence for the act of killing.
"If one just casually checks a few boxes on paper or presses a button to complete the execution, then those holding judgment power will quickly lose the sense of reality about killing, making them more likely to make less careful judgments.
"Just like how Jiang He decided to kill the first male criminal who caused death through negligence: if she knew in advance she’d have to do it personally, she very likely wouldn’t have made the death penalty judgment."
Yang Yuting still didn’t quite understand, "But why would this relate to ’consistency voting’?"
Lin Sizhi continued, "Because although ’judgment consistency’ is somewhat stricter than the concept of ’fairness,’ it’s not completely without ambiguous space.
"Just as in ’King’s Judgment,’ the king could publicly announce prisoners’ crimes and create associations with the prisoner rooms to change some audience members’ views;
"’Childbirth Judgment’ actually has a similar mechanism, only it’s not done by speaking but by personally taking action.
"After making a death penalty judgment, the Chief Judge’s behavior also affects the audience’s impression of her.
"If she dares to personally execute the judgment and bear all consequences for her decision, then a small portion of the audience might approve of her more, which also helps ’consistency voting.’
"Conversely, if she doesn’t dare personally execute the judgment and pushes this responsibility to others, that’s adding to the crime. The double standards in judgment become more obviously exposed. Even those who favor her can’t deceive themselves into giving biased votes.
"Of course, this mechanism ultimately only wins over swing votes and doesn’t work on audience members with firm convictions."

chapters.title: Chapter 193: Li Jiang’s Vote
chapters.content:
Zheng Jie suddenly had a flash of inspiration, "Hey, I just thought of a possibility.
"Since this game can be cleared by just voting one person to death, could it work like this?
"From the beginning, there’s no need to complete the reproduction task. We just need to save only the worst serious offender among all the criminals. Then, after triggering the barbarian invasion, the four judgment team players vote him to death, and we successfully clear the game.
"Then the four people get the full 300,000 visa time reward, over 70,000 per person."
Yang Yuting looked a bit confused, "But isn’t that a bit too much of a god’s eye view?"
Cai Zhiyuan shook his head, "This method won’t work.
"In theory it’s perfect, but in actual operation there are too many variables.
"Because the voting order in this game was carefully designed by the God’s Imitator, look."
He pointed again at the rule details on the large screen.
"The final voting follows this order:"First are the two assistants.
"Second are the two players forced into the game.
"Last are the released criminals.
"If an extra criminal is released, they are judged last.
"Taking this game’s situation as an example, if our community adopted this strategy, then Community 13 would have many opportunities in the game to secretly hint to the criminal, getting the criminal to vote with them to kill the two players from Community 17.
"In this situation, the criminal’s 1 vote would instead become the key swing vote. Whichever side he stands on becomes the majority.
"Of course, if the criminal votes with Community 13’s players to kill the two people from Community 17, he would definitely also be voted to death by Community 13’s players in the end.
"But regardless, keeping a criminal who committed a serious crime and is cunning and treacherous until the very end, placing hope in trust between two unfamiliar communities, this is by no means wise behavior.
"Any deviation in any link, or even possibly just a random impulse from this criminal, could lead to disastrous consequences."
Zheng Jie thought for a moment, "What if we watch each other and don’t allow anyone to approach the criminal privately?"
Cai Zhiyuan shook his head, "That’s also useless. The criminal won’t just wait for death, he would very likely figure out this logic himself.
"Moreover, what if the other community gets desperate and plays their cards openly? They just blatantly tell the criminal to vote you all to death together. What methods do you have to restrain the other party’s behavior?"
Zheng Jie nodded in sudden understanding. Indeed, this method was really quite unreliable.
The premise for completing this plan was that the two communities had sufficient mutual trust, but if they had that kind of mutual trust, wouldn’t it be better to just play the game properly?
Creating reproduction badges could also clear the game, so why insist on going to the final step, placing fate in the hope of a completely unreliable death vote.
Cai Zhiyuan continued, "Actually, Li Jiang killing Fei Xiong in the end was also due to voting reasons.
"Li Jiang ultimately chose to vote Chen Xin to death, so his saving Chen Xin definitely wasn’t out of heroic righteousness.
"On the surface, if it’s a choice between Fei Xiong and Chen Xin entering the final vote, Fei Xiong is male and Chen Xin is female, so the probability of Fei Xiong voting Li Jiang to death would be lower.
"But if someone really thinks this way, then they’ve been brainwashed by gender narratives. Who says a man definitely won’t vote to kill another man?
"A murderous maniac like Fei Xiong was already crazy. He very likely would directly vote ’death’ for everyone. Li Jiang even let him use torture devices several times, so how could he possibly show Li Jiang any mercy?
"So Li Jiang definitely wouldn’t allow Fei Xiong to live and vote.
"Looking at Chen Xin on the other hand, although she was a female player, Li Jiang saved her life. The person directly responsible for the game’s failure was Jiang He, who served as the Chief Judge.
"Between Li Jiang and Jiang He, Chen Xin would most likely protect Li Jiang and vote for Jiang He.
"As for why Li Jiang, Chen Yumei, and Zhao Dong voted to kill Chen Xin in the end?
"Because the visa time reward in this game is divided equally among all surviving players. The more people who die, the fewer people to split the money.
"After Li Jiang and Chen Yumei confirmed they were already safe, they would naturally choose to vote to kill Chen Xin and Zhao Dong, the two criminals judged last, as much as possible.
"At this point, for Zhao Dong, if she voted ’life’ for Chen Xin, with three votes keeping Chen Xin alive, then when it was Zhao Dong’s turn to be judged, Chen Xin would most likely vote her to death to get a bigger share.
"Conversely, if Zhao Dong voted Chen Xin to ’death’, when it was her turn to be judged, only four people would vote. As long as Yang Yuting voted ’life’ for her, she would definitely survive.
"So Zhao Dong couldn’t place her life in Chen Xin’s great kindness. The only choice was to vote Chen Xin to ’death’.
"This is a bit like the logic problem of ’pirates dividing gold coins’. The criminals actually don’t have many choices."
Yang Yuting nodded in sudden understanding, "I see... I was wondering earlier, since Li Jiang was chosen by Chen Yumei as an assistant to enter the judgment game, he should be a fairly strong player in Community 13.
"But throughout the entire game, I didn’t see him being particularly proactive.
"So this was the strategy."
Cai Zhiyuan said, "I think Li Jiang probably isn’t the type of player with very strong ability to break through situations. He mostly adopts stable strategies.
"With Jiang He as the Chief Judge and having a rather negative opinion of him, his suggestions would most likely not be adopted, so it’s better to go with the flow. A weak identity also has its own way of playing.
"’Chief Judge’ is an advantageous identity, but it also means that if the game fails, they will bear the greatest responsibility.
"Once voting starts, the ’Chief Judge’ is the easiest to die.
"Li Jiang didn’t need to ensure game victory, he just needed to ensure that he and Chen Yumei appropriately built up some goodwill, lowered their presence a bit, and weren’t voted to death first in the end."
Yang Yuting grabbed her hair somewhat frantically, all grace abandoned, "So that means Jiang He really did step into quite a few traps in this game, and precisely walked onto the only death path planned by the God’s Imitator...
"But there’s one thing I still can’t figure out. Although choosing either mechanism 1 or mechanism 2 was about the same, why did she insist on having women tied to mechanism 1?"
Everyone fell into silence.
Obviously, to explain this issue clearly, one couldn’t just start from the game mechanics, but had to comprehensively analyze Jiang He as a person but most of the people present didn’t actually know her particularly well, so they couldn’t make particularly accurate analyses either.
Li Renshu took over, "Just right, I should also explain the issue of the death immunity token.
"When everyone decided to entrust the death immunity token to me for safekeeping, I did promise that the use of the death immunity token wouldn’t particularly distinguish between the strong and weak. Whoever encounters a death risk first gets to use it.
"However, I did not violate my political commitment.
"Because I also said there would be situations where I wouldn’t save someone, mainly three types:
"First is destroying the community’s stability and unity.
"Second is acting willfully in a game and not executing team strategy.
"Third is making clear betrayal behavior in a game.
"I may not be able to think of other situations comprehensively, but if there are situations with destructive power roughly equal to these three, it’s also possible I won’t save them.
"Of course, if it’s other bad behavior with harm far less than these three types, I would most likely still choose to save them, leaving the final judgment to the two players who hold veto power."
Fu Chen hesitated, "You mean to say that Jiang He acted willfully in the game and didn’t execute the ’kill all’ strategy we gave?
"But at that time, the people inside couldn’t distinguish which specific strategy came from our community.
"Or are you saying she didn’t accept Yang Yuting’s suggestion?
"But between her and Yang Yuting, there was no clear decision-making priority.
"If Lawyer Lin and Jiang He entered the game and she didn’t listen to Lawyer Lin’s suggestions, we could say this was not executing team strategy, but Yang Yuting’s suggestions haven’t reached that level of weight, have they?
"We can’t think about this problem from a god’s eye view.
"Jiang He encountered a judgment game with extremely strong targeting. It could be said that stepping into traps was a high-probability event. If we decide not to save someone because of this, then if other people also encounter targeted judgment games and also step into traps, should we not save any of them?
"Of course, judging from everyone’s attitude, perhaps everyone accepts this result, but I still hope these standards can be more clear."
Li Renshu shook her head, "No, I chose not to save her not entirely because of the second reason, but also because of the first.
"I believe Jiang He’s existence would destroy the community’s stability and unity. Her ideological tendencies are dangerous. Or rather, she’s actually already making some similar attempts.
"I made this decision based on these two points combined."
Fu Chen was stunned, "Destroying the community’s stability and unity? How so?"
Hearing this statement, Wang Yongxin’s brow twitched, his expression becoming slightly unnatural.
If Li Renshu viewed any private group formation outside the five-person group as ’destroying community stability and unity’, then his behavior obviously counted too.
Could it be that when he encounters danger, Li Renshu won’t save him either?
However, what Li Renshu said next made Wang Yongxin feel much more at ease.
Li Renshu continued to explain, "Everyone, please don’t misunderstand. I’m not saying the community doesn’t allow private group protests or opposing voices.
"Each of us has an equal vote, so whether it’s expressing opposing opinions or forming groups to vote and influence community proposals, these are rights we should have.
"What I mean by destroying community stability and unity mainly refers to some values and ideological tendencies whose destructive and divisive effects are significantly greater than their positive effects.
"For example, I believe Jiang He has very obvious gender narrative tendencies, and she’s been making attempts around these tendencies all along."
Xu Tong was very puzzled, "Wait, is there such a thing?
"Jiang He has hardly participated in community proposal discussions before, right?
"Gender narrative, do you mean she has feminist thoughts? But that’s not really a capital offense, is it? If we really have to say, don’t we all have some of that to varying degrees?
"Whether it’s feminism or masculinism, as long as it doesn’t harm others, shouldn’t it all be everyone’s freedom?"
Li Renshu nodded, "Yes, on this point, I acknowledge that everyone’s thoughts are free.
"Feminism or masculinism, as long as it doesn’t affect others, it doesn’t matter what you believe in.
"Just like how Brother Wang believes capital is supreme, while some people hate the wealthy. These are also two opposing values, but as long as they don’t seriously infringe on other community members’ interests and can be reconciled, then the community should remain neutral on this issue.
"But Jiang He has obviously been frequently attempting to use gender narratives to influence the community’s political activities recently. You may not feel it very obviously, but as a party involved, I can feel it very clearly."

chapters.title: Chapter 194: The Reason for the Change
chapters.content:
Many people still looked confused. Obviously, most people hadn’t noticed what Li Renshu was talking about.
In their impression, Jiang He was just a not-too-smart, somewhat low-EQ peripheral figure. Her abilities were indeed not particularly outstanding, but she was usually kind to others and could even be said to have a somewhat helpful image.
How could she have such serious problems in Li Renshu’s eyes?
Li Renshu sighed quietly, "To be honest, I don’t understand why this situation occurred either.
"Jiang He’s behavior only appeared recently, and it once shocked me greatly. I even thought she had been possessed by someone.
"I thought about it for a long time but couldn’t figure out why she would suddenly undergo this kind of change."
Everyone looked at each other, no one speaking.
Li Renshu could be said to be the person with the strongest political consciousness in all of Community 17. If even she found it puzzling, the others would only be more confused.
Lin Sizhi was silent for a moment, then said, "I actually think you’re overthinking this problem.
"You projected your own political literacy onto Jiang He, so you completely couldn’t understand why she would have such vastly different behavior before and after."But Jiang He’s change may very likely just be due to a very simple reason:
"Before she believed you had become the community’s power core, in her eyes, the community was controlled by male players like Fu Chen, Cai Zhiyuan, Officer Cao, and you as the only woman were in a subordinate state.
"So she hurriedly hid her tendencies and intentions, not daring to let other people in the community discover them.
"Later, she realized you had already become the community’s power core and believed the conditions were ripe, so she actively and eagerly wanted to participate in the community’s politics.
"I think this is the only reason for Jiang He’s change."
Li Renshu was stunned. She frowned and pondered for a moment, then nodded with understanding.
"Indeed, I was overthinking it... Lawyer Lin’s explanation is very likely the only reasonable one."
This topic made the atmosphere in the hall somewhat heavy. Obviously, this was the first time the sensitive topic of ’power core’ was being discussed publicly.
Previous discussions were all conducted privately in small groups but this was something that would happen sooner or later anyway.
On one hand, almost everyone in the community had already connected privately and more or less confirmed the existence of the five-person group. This was no longer such a big secret.
On the other hand, since they were discussing Jiang He’s matter, it was inevitable to explain this topic clearly and thoroughly.
Otherwise, people in the community without such sensitive political awareness wouldn’t understand why Li Renshu made such a decision, and this problem would become a thorn lodged in the flesh.
Cai Zhiyuan said, "On this point, I support Renshu’s decision.
"My assessment of Jiang He is: her heart is not bad, she’s not smart, and her political ability is not strong either. However, her political sensitivity is very high.
"When ’weak political ability’ and ’high political sensitivity’ both appear in the same person, they will exhibit this kind of somewhat split, self-contradictory behavior.
"Regarding the ’high political sensitivity’ point, I can give a few simple examples. Everyone think about whether this is the case.
"Shortly after entering the community, when everyone wasn’t very familiar yet, Jiang He was already actively getting close to Li Renshu.
"After that, in almost every proposal, although Jiang He didn’t participate much in discussions, she was always the first to express her position and vote.
"In ’Blood Poker’, Jiang He also spontaneously took on the role of leader to communicate and cooperate with Community 3.
"Also, during our first recruitment, even though the male-female ratio was 5:6, she still clearly proposed the demand to recruit women.
"I’m not evaluating whether these things were right or wrong. I’m just saying that these behaviors are all manifestations of ’high political sensitivity’."
Everyone recalled separately, then nodded one after another.
These things did indeed leave some impression.
Taking out any single incident alone didn’t really prove anything but with so many things together, it was hard to explain with pure coincidence.
Wang Yongxin frowned, "So Jiang He’s behavior is indeed somewhat self-contradictory.
"Being the first to vote every time represents her intention to actively participate in proposal discussions. However, every time proposals are discussed, she doesn’t speak.
"Our atmosphere for discussing proposals is very relaxed, not serious, and in most cases, people can speak freely.
"This shows she’s not that she doesn’t want to speak, but that she doesn’t dare to.
"When Fu Chen was chairing proposals, she worried that expressing political views would expose her, that she would be excluded and targeted, so she chose to hide herself, not express opinions, only expressing her support at the end when voting after the dust had settled.
"As Li Renshu chaired more proposals, Jiang He believed her thoughts would no longer be rejected by the community, and might even become mainstream with Li Renshu’s support.
"So she started expressing her demands more directly, especially when discussing with Li Renshu one-on-one privately.
"Of course, Jiang He’s behavior might have some lag. On one hand, it might be because she couldn’t accurately judge the specific time when Li Renshu became the core, and on the other hand, it might be for the sake of caution.
"But regardless, after she confirmed this point, she began to no longer hide her thoughts. That’s why it gives people the feeling of ’suddenly becoming a different person’."
Li Renshu continued, "I think it’s necessary to emphasize again that our community should be maximally tolerant of different political views.
"Regarding feminist views, frankly speaking, I also agree with many aspects. Similarly, if certain players in the community hold extreme masculinist views, as long as they don’t affect community stability, other people have no right to interfere.
"On this point, members of our community should have full freedom of choice. Believe in whatever you want to believe.
"However, we absolutely cannot allow any single narrative to invade our community’s political life and become mainstream."
Li Renshu paused slightly, then continued:
"All identity narratives, in my view, are single narratives.
"And gender narrative, among all identity narratives, is the worst kind, because it directly leads to half the people opposing the other half.
"The fewer people in a political entity, the more unstable it is, the more it lacks margin for error.
"If it were a country with tens of millions or even hundreds of millions of people, then although a single narrative would also bring some unstable tendencies, ultimately because the volume is large enough, it wouldn’t immediately produce such obvious destructive effects.
"But our community only has 12 people. If any single narrative gains the upper hand, stability will cease to exist, leaving only endless chaos and infighting.
"So if Jiang He hadn’t encountered a life-and-death crisis in the game, it would be difficult for us to actively kick her out. We could only try our best to bridge this divide and repair the possible damage.
"But if she encountered a life-and-death crisis in the game, I also couldn’t use the death immunity token bought by all community members to save her.
"Of course, ultimately this is a subjective judgment I made, and I’m willing to take full responsibility for it.
"If everyone feels this judgment is inappropriate, we can also vote again to entrust the death immunity token to someone else for safekeeping."

chapters.title: Chapter 195: The Issue of Fairness
chapters.content:
The hall fell into silence for a moment.
Wang Yongxin spoke first, "I think this judgment is fine."
After serious consideration, Qin Yao also nodded, "I also think it’s fine."
As for the others, it was hard to say whether they were satisfied with this decision or not, but at least no one openly opposed it.
So there was no need to actually vote.
This result was naturally within Li Renshu’s expectations.
A mature politician wouldn’t initiate a vote unfavorable to themselves unless they were completely certain of the voting outcome.
For Wang Yongxin, expressing support was the only choice he could make right now.
Interestingly, Wang Yongxin did a simple deduction and discovered that this incident actually had three different possibilities:
Fu Chen controls the death immunity token and decides to save someone.Li Renshu controls the death immunity token and decides to save someone.
Li Renshu controls the death immunity token and decides not to save someone.
Among these three possibilities, if Wang Yongxin had to choose himself, the second would be the most optimistic situation.
If Fu Chen saved her, Wang Yongxin would definitely have to use his veto power, but that would be equivalent to him being the villain. Considering his own gender and limited political prestige, it would be difficult to provide as proper an explanation as Li Renshu’s, which would further damage his already limited popularity.
If Li Renshu saved her, that would be best for Wang Yongxin.
Because he could use this opportunity to question Li Renshu’s "standards for using the death immunity token," create some rifts within the five-person group, and expand his own voice, causing certain players to further distance themselves from Li Renshu and lean toward him.
But obviously, Li Renshu wouldn’t make such a low-level mistake, ultimately leading to a result that for Wang Yongxin was neither good nor bad.
Regarding this result, Wang Yongxin could only accept and support it.
Entrusting this token to different people for management each had advantages and disadvantages. There was no perfect choice.
This also made Wang Yongxin feel somewhat dramatic: at the time, his proposal was for Fu Chen to manage the death immunity token. If it really had been Fu Chen managing it, then there was a high probability he would have used it for Jiang He.
As for whether it would be vetoed, that was another matter, but at least there wouldn’t be a situation where it wasn’t used at all.
It was Jiang He who clearly expressed support for Li Renshu, but conversely, it was Li Renshu who decided not to use it for her.
It was somewhat sigh-inducing.
Cai Zhiyuan realized this topic could end, so he pointed at the large screen again.
"Actually, speaking of this, everyone can better understand the decisions Jiang He made in the game.
"When choosing an assistant, the reason she insisted on not bringing Aunt Zhou but bringing Yang Yuting was mainly based on two considerations.
"First, she viewed this game as an opportunity to prove herself, so she decided to leave this opportunity to Yang Yuting, whom she believed had a closer ideology.
"Second, she may indeed have learned some knowledge related to reproduction due to her work, but obviously, the knowledge she learned and the knowledge tested in the game were misaligned."
Yang Yuting was shocked, "Wait, what do you mean closer ideology!"
Cai Zhiyuan explained, "Because Aunt Zhou is older, it’s impossible for her to share the same ideology.
"In Jiang He’s eyes, the ranking of closeness between her and the other female players in the community was probably like this: Li Renshu, you, Xu Tong, Qin Yao, Aunt Zhou.
"You and Jiang He are similar in age, so she naturally believed you held the same views as her and naturally stood on her side.
"She just overlooked one thing: family environment.
"Your original family was too wealthy, so you’re more similar to Qin Yao. You’re both beneficiaries of the old system’s gender division of labor, so in terms of ideological tendencies, you two have great differences from Jiang He.
"This difference is determined by economic foundation and life experience.
"Simply put: the poorer the original family, the more likely women are to be harmed under the original gender division of labor, and they will naturally have stronger feminist tendencies. Conversely, the wealthier the original family, the more likely women are to benefit under the original gender division of labor, thus developing resistance to feminism.
"Frankly speaking, gender conflicts are sharper at the lower levels and more moderate at the upper levels. Essentially, it’s gender-based mutual harm caused by insufficient resources at the lower levels.
"So when Jiang He saw your answers to those initial 5 questions, she must have been very surprised."
Yang Yuting was speechless for a moment. She understood a bit why Jiang He had been overly enthusiastic toward her.
Obviously both sides had somewhat misunderstood each other.
Yang Yuting thought for a moment, then asked again, "Then what you said about Jiang He having done some research on reproduction issues, but the knowledge she learned and the knowledge tested in the game being misaligned, what does that mean?
"I think the three questions tested in the game were all very basic questions, right?
"Right, Aunt Zhou?"
Zhou Guifen nodded, "I think they’re quite basic.
"You don’t even necessarily need childcare experience. Buy a childcare reference book and you can find answers to all these questions."
Cai Zhiyuan explained, "So I said this is actually a kind of knowledge structure misalignment.
"Jiang He’s profession is editor, which inevitably involves some hot topics, which certainly include gender issues and reproduction issues.
"But when discussing these topics in newspapers, magazines, or new media, they generally don’t involve specific ’practical operation’ aspects.
"For example, when we discuss fertility rate topics online, who would discuss specifically how many scoops of formula to mix for newborns? Everyone subconsciously ignores it.
"But in actual reproduction issues, these details are crucial.
"It can also be said that whether they’re policymakers or people discussing these topics, what they’re actually discussing isn’t the topic itself, but just using this topic to freely express other views they want to express.
"This game precisely captured this point, accurately distinguishing between people who ’think they understand reproduction’ and people who ’truly understand reproduction’.
"Those people who repeatedly mention reproduction topics but don’t even understand basic common sense in the actual nurturing process are actually just using reproduction issues to profit themselves, whether male or female.
"Of course, I must honestly say I don’t know these questions either, but I also don’t care about this topic.
"Obviously in the view of the God’s Imitator who designed this game, compared to people who genuinely don’t know or understand, those who claim to know but don’t actually grasp the details are more worthy targets of judgment."
Yang Yuting sighed quietly, "Okay, let’s stop this topic here. I don’t really want to discuss it anymore."
She somewhat helplessly realized that Jiang He’s situation seemed consistent inside and outside the game.
In the game, Jiang He presumptuously treated all female players as "her people." In the community, she similarly presumptuously treated Li Renshu as "her person."
In the end, it was the "her people" inside the game who voted to kill her, and the "her person" outside the game who decided not to use the token to save her.
Were they really her people?
Not necessarily.
The female players in the game considered whether Jiang He could lead them to successfully clear the game, or rather, clear the game in the simplest and most reliable way.
In the community, Li Renshu considered the community’s stability, giving corresponding status only after players made sufficiently large contributions.
This was the first priority. They didn’t care whether this person was specifically male or female.
Just like Community 3 and Community 4, Lu Xinyi and Han Mengying could become the core of their communities not because of their gender, but because of their actual abilities.
After thinking for a long time, Zheng Jie raised a new question, "Then ultimately, this judgment game isn’t fair either.
"Chen Yumei and Jiang He committed the same crime, but the one who hid deeper survived instead?
"Moreover, those criminals who were tied up had all received legal judgments. But if the judgment team members decided to kill them in exchange for reproduction funds, they had absolutely no power to fight back and could only wait for death.
"That’s also not quite reasonable, right?"
Everyone said in unison, "Don’t consider fairness issues in judgment games."
Zheng Jie was stunned. Obviously, this was a conclusion everyone had reached when discussing "King’s Judgment," and he wasn’t in the community yet at that time.
Wang Yongxin sighed, "Actually strictly speaking, all judgment games that have appeared so far, all of them, are unfair.
"Games involving fewer people might be relatively better, but they’re still unfair.
"And the more people involved in a judgment game, the less it has to do with fairness.
"So don’t have any special filter for judgment games just because you see the word ’judgment.’ The judgment in your concept and the judgment the Gallery considers are very likely two completely different things.
"In King’s Judgment, did the crimes of Zhang Peng, Gao Zhankui, myself, and Cai Zhiyuan reach the point where we had to die?
"But if the King really wanted to kill us, we had no negotiating space either.
"Of course, on the surface, we could obtain the King identity through ’Farmer’s Walk,’ or lighter punishment by persuading the King, seemingly providing a tiny bit of surface-level negotiating space, slightly better than the criminals in ’Childbirth Judgment’ who were locked up and couldn’t even speak.
"But is there any essential difference?
"There isn’t.
"All other judgment games are the same. They’ve never been fair.
"We can only say that on this point, all God’s Imitators share the same understanding."

chapters.title: Chapter 196: The God’s Imitator’s Discretionary Power
chapters.content:
After thinking for a moment, Cao Haichuan said, "I actually think this isn’t the God’s Imitators’ tacit understanding, but rather the inevitable result of the Gallery’s mechanism.
"Suppose we now want to throw many criminals into the same game for judgment, then this will definitely be an unfair game.
"Because if it were fair, it would mean each criminal has an equal chance of winning. They would each display their abilities, and the nature of the game would become closer to ’distribution-type’ or ’screening-type’ games.
"To dig pits for specific people, or to judge specific themes, you must give some criminals extra privileges, making them advantageous identities.
"With advantageous identities, naturally there are disadvantaged identities, and even pure cannon fodder identities waiting to die.
"The ’cannon fodder’ in judgment must also be played by real players, not replaced with false files, because that wouldn’t serve the purpose of ’testing human nature’.
"Who would be stupid enough to expose their weaknesses to a bunch of false files? As long as they’re not crazy, everyone can make rational choices.
"Only when the cannon fodder are also real players will the advantaged identity players fall into the judgment game’s trap.
"When the Gallery wants to judge a specific theme, it must give the God’s Imitator sufficiently large ’discretionary power’. The more the Gallery encourages God’s Imitators to make distinctive designs, the greater this ’discretionary power’ must be.
"God’s Imitators can forcibly save certain criminals, and can also forcibly wrongfully kill certain criminals."This is the God’s Imitator’s privilege. We can only accept this privilege and prepare ourselves mentally: perhaps truly fair judgment games will never appear."
After considering for a moment, Cai Zhiyuan said, "Actually, if we must say something, I do have a speculation.
"That is, when the Gallery issues judgment tasks, there very likely exists some kind of indirect screening mechanism."
Everyone was stunned, "Indirect screening mechanism? What do you mean?"
Cai Zhiyuan explained, "Let’s assume that when God’s Imitators create judgment games and select criminals, they are completely free and can see a list of criminals from all communities in the entire New World.
"What kind of result would this produce?
"God’s Imitators would only need to design a game, throw their enemies into positions where they must die, and they could easily kill everyone they want to kill.
"The Gallery might show some favoritism toward God’s Imitators, but not to this extent.
"So I believe that when the Gallery selects judgment targets, there is also a priority order.
"For example, people whom the Gallery considers to have lower value and should be eliminated first will be prioritized as judgment targets and assigned to God’s Imitators.
"The first three real judgment targets in our community were Uncle Ding, Aunt Su, and Jiang He.
"Is this purely coincidental? I don’t think so.
"If we were to evaluate ’Community 17 player value’, these three would happen to be the lowest.
"Besides this, I think from the situation in this ’Childbirth Judgment’, those criminals locked on the wall without much negotiating space were very likely also targets the Gallery considered should be eliminated first.
"So I think we might as well propose this hypothesis:
"The more the Gallery considers a player to have lower value to the New World, the more likely they are to become targets of judgment games. Moreover, the more likely they are to play purely ’cannon fodder’ roles in judgment games."
Wang Yongxin was stunned, "Then what was the situation with us two in ’King’s Judgment’?"
Cai Zhiyuan explained, "We two were probably dragged down by Uncle Ding, since we happened to belong to the same case.
"Xu Tong and Aunt Su are in a similar situation."
Everyone fell into silence. Obviously, Cai Zhiyuan’s statement did make some sense.
The relatively clear fact was the priority of judgment games.
According to the Gallery’s standards, it could almost be said that everyone has original sin, and all people in Community 17 should have their own judgment games.
The reason they haven’t yet couldn’t possibly be the God’s Imitators’ great mercy. The only reason was that the Gallery hadn’t issued relevant requirements.
As long as the Gallery issued them, there would definitely be clever God’s Imitators who would design the games. There’s no escaping.
So were the first three main judgment targets being Ding Wenqiang, Su Xiucen, and Jiang He a coincidence?
Obviously not.
These three had one thing in common. It wasn’t simply being weak, stubborn, or incompatible with the community environment, but rather ’lower value’.
This so-called value was the value judged by the New World, which could be seen from the difference in ’initial visa time’.
It might include multiple factors, such as age, personality, professional background, knowledge system, moral standards, and so on.
Currently, no one knew what the specific standards were.
But from those criminals in ’Childbirth Judgment’ who had little negotiating space, it could also be roughly determined that their value to the Gallery was most likely lower than the four main players.
They very likely had little initial visa time, committed serious crimes, didn’t quite understand the community and New World rules, and didn’t earn much visa time afterward either.
In the Gallery’s eyes, they were originally targets to be cleaned up first, so the Gallery allowed God’s Imitators to use them as ’cannon fodder’ in judgment games.
Lin Sizhi couldn’t help but think of Wei Xinjian, whom the Gallery threw to him for testing before entering the game.
During the testing process, Wei Xinjian was also completely passive. Although Lin Sizhi left him room to survive, if Lin Sizhi had designed the game more harshly and lowered the rating to B, unreasonably killing Wei Xinjian, it would most likely still pass the review.
Having absolutely no way to survive wouldn’t work, but whether the way to survive was large or small completely depended on the God’s Imitator.
The Gallery’s attitude toward different players was clearly divided into several completely different standards.
Among the two identities of God’s Imitator and player, there were similar labels like ’excellent’, ’average’, and ’terrible’.
The lower this label, the worse the situation for the God’s Imitator or player.
If evaluated by the Gallery as a ’terrible player’ or ’low-value player’, then not only would they be judged first, but they would also very likely be arranged by the God’s Imitator in purely expendable corner positions waiting to die in the judgment.
The Gallery would approve this kind of arrangement.
Conversely, if a God’s Imitator put high-value players in ’cannon fodder’ positions, the Gallery would most likely not approve.
Li Renshu gave the final summary statement, "So, to encounter ’judgment games’ later, or to not be arranged as ’cannon fodder’ in ’judgment games’, the only way is to prove your value as much as possible before the judgment game arrives, and not become a ’low-value player’ in the Gallery’s eyes.
"If the Gallery really wants to judge Lawyer Lin someday, then I believe it will also be after everyone in the entire community has been judged once, and Lawyer Lin will definitely get the greatest advantageous identity in the judgment game."
Lin Sizhi smiled faintly, "Is that so? That’s really good news."
Everyone sighed quietly.
This screening mechanism was very cruel, but from the Gallery’s standpoint, it was quite reasonable.
Qin Yao raised her hand and asked, "I have a question.
"Could ’Childbirth Judgment’ and ’King’s Judgment’... be works by the same God’s Imitator?"
Everyone fell into silence.
Obviously, this question hit the mark. Most people present also wanted to ask this question.
Xu Tong thought for a moment, "Obviously yes, right? There’s a strong sense of déjà vu everywhere!
"There are inner field players and spectators, there’s an evaluation mechanism, there are different torture devices, and there’s extremely strong targeting of advantageous identities...
"It’s almost like they were carved from the same mold.
"It just played some new tricks based on ’King’s Judgment’, but the design thinking is obviously consistent."
Li Renshu looked at Cao Haichuan, "I think this question should be asked to a professional.
"Officer Cao, do you think it was done by the same God’s Imitator?"
Cao Haichuan thought for a while. Obviously, this question didn’t have a very definite answer for him either and required careful response.
"I’m actually more inclined to think they’re not the same God’s Imitator.
"The designer of ’Childbirth Judgment’ is more like a ’God’s Imitator’s imitator’."

chapters.title: Chapter 197: A Speculation
chapters.content:
Xu Tong was somewhat surprised, "A God’s Imitator’s imitator?"
Obviously, most people hadn’t thought that such a concept could exist before.
Cao Haichuan paused slightly, then explained:
"I believe we cannot simply assume two games are the work of the same God’s Imitator just because they’re similar.
"In fact, quite the opposite. I’m inclined to think that the more similar the games are, the less likely they’re by the same God’s Imitator.
"Why would there be ’God’s Imitators’ imitators’?
"Because the rules of all games so far have been public. Since all players can see them, then God’s Imitators hidden among the players can naturally see them too.
"’King’s Judgment’ received an S-level rating, so it will not only become an object of study for players, but will inevitably also become a key learning point for God’s Imitators.
"If a God’s Imitator is relatively clever, they can transform and apply the core concept, achieving a state of spiritual similarity without physical similarity. But if a God’s Imitator isn’t that clever, then the traces of imitation will be heavier, and there may be a lot of déjà vu.
"So we cannot assert that two works are by the same God’s Imitator simply because they’re ’similar’."Just like many serial murder cases in reality, there are many cases of copycat crimes. If we determine they’re by the same criminal just because they’re ’similar’, we’ll often fall into serious misunderstandings."
Everyone had different expressions. Some nodded, some remained silent.
But regardless, coming from Cao Haichuan, these words were quite convincing.
Wang Yongxin frowned slightly, "Here’s the problem. If there are ’God’s Imitators’ imitators’, which now seems like a high-probability event, doesn’t this also mean we can almost never distinguish which two games are specifically the work of the same God’s Imitator?"
Li Renshu also asked, "Then Officer Cao, based on what considerations do you believe ’Childbirth Judgment’ is the work of a ’God’s Imitator’s imitator’?"
Cao Haichuan explained, "Motive. Ultimately, we still have to fall back on the God’s Imitator’s motive. That’s the most reliable method.
"If two games are only similar in rules, then there are simply two possibilities:
"The first possibility is that this is the work of the original God’s Imitator, who was just lazy, borrowed the original design thinking, changed some details, and created a new game.
"This possibility does exist, but we must consider that a God’s Imitator capable of creating an S-level game must be very clever and very good at hiding themselves.
"What great benefit would they get from making another similar game? The disadvantages are quite obvious: an overly distinctive design style would very likely make them easier to expose and be targeted by players.
"For a God’s Imitator, this is unsafe. Designing games with completely different styles each time would be better camouflage.
"The second possibility is that other God’s Imitators imitated their style and made similar designs. And the original God’s Imitator is powerless to stop this.
"For the later imitator, this behavior has all benefits and no harm: it can mislead players, pushing the hatred onto the first God’s Imitator, while also improving the competitiveness of their own game.
"So from a motive standpoint, does the God’s Imitator who designed ’King’s Judgment’ have more motive to create such a similar game? Or do other God’s Imitators have more motive?"
Everyone nodded in sudden understanding.
This was indeed a point they hadn’t thought of before.
Cao Haichuan’s deduction contained an important preset premise: God’s Imitators all try their best to hide themselves.
From what they could see so far, this preset premise held true in most cases.
So those relatively excellent God’s Imitators, whether designing A-level or S-level games, were definitely clever people who would carefully hide themselves.
When not urgently short on visa time, rashly using previous game frameworks to design would increase the risk of exposure. This wouldn’t be wise behavior.
Even if they wanted to make new games to achieve certain specific purposes, they would definitely try to distance themselves from previous games as much as possible.
They might even deliberately design some low-rated games as decoys.
Although from what they could see now, it was difficult for players to trace who specifically was a God’s Imitator based solely on game rules, or even guess which games were made by the same God’s Imitator.
But who could say for sure about the future?
There were many players like Cao Haichuan who were good at finding clues from subtle traces. Minute habits inadvertently revealed by God’s Imitators could all potentially become fatal flaws that expose their identity someday.
The cleverer the God’s Imitator, the less likely they would be to consecutively design similar games.
Although it couldn’t be proven at all, because it was built on some relatively solid reasoning, it could still convince many people.
Wang Yongxin thought for a moment, "We mentioned before that when God’s Imitators design games, they’re very likely to tend to utilize their existing knowledge systems.
"Just like ’Blind Date Game’.
"So could the God’s Imitator of ’Childbirth Judgment’ also be relatively experienced in this area?
"Maybe a more traditional, older male or female image? Otherwise it would be hard to come up with those three questions that hit young people’s knowledge blind spots, right?"
Cao Haichuan shook his head, "Hard to say. These three questions in Childbirth Judgment are indeed very difficult for players who haven’t learned the corresponding knowledge.
"But they’re not difficult for God’s Imitators, since they’re the ones asking the questions.
"Don’t forget, there’s a library area in the community with all kinds of books covering everything.
"As the answering party, of course there’s no way to find the corresponding answers from the vast sea of books. But it’s different if you’re the questioning party.
"A God’s Imitator just needs to find a time when no one’s around, go to the library area and casually flip through some reproduction-related books, and randomly pick a few questions.
"They don’t necessarily need to draw from their existing knowledge system.
"Of course, from the game content, this God’s Imitator should be relatively sensitive to gender issues and reproduction issues, but we didn’t see any particularly obvious tendencies. And even if there were, such tendencies would be relatively easy to hide."
Yang Yuting said, "Jiang He previously thought Li Jiang was the God’s Imitator for this game. What do you all think?"
Lin Sizhi shook his head, "Doesn’t seem like it.
"Zhong Yuanyuan participated in ’Blind Date Game’ because she confirmed she was absolutely safe in the game, and needed to work with others from Community 1 to stir up hatred and kill more players to earn visa time.
"That is, simultaneously satisfying both ’safety’ and ’profitable’ conditions.
"But Li Jiang in ’Childbirth Judgment’ didn’t meet either condition.
"He was neither absolutely safe nor able to gain much benefit from it.
"If Li Jiang were the God’s Imitator, the only explanation would be finding some excitement for himself.
"Jiang He felt Li Jiang’s words were confrontational and misled her into making some wrong decisions, but that was actually a bit of a misunderstanding."
Yang Yuting asked again, "What about Chen Yumei?"
Lin Sizhi still shook his head, "I don’t think that’s very likely either."
Fu Chen nodded in agreement, "Right, how could a God’s Imitator judge themselves? That would be too absurd."
Cao Haichuan provided a timely reminder, "The Gallery never said God’s Imitators can’t judge themselves. Although I also think this possibility is small, we can’t simply and crudely rule it out."
Lin Sizhi explained, "Although Chen Yumei seems to have escaped judgment, I don’t think this is quite like ’the God’s Imitator’s way’."

chapters.title: Chapter 198: Considerations for Recruitment
chapters.content:
Fu Chen didn’t quite understand. After thinking for a moment, he said, "You mean if Chen Yumei were the God’s Imitator, she could actually become the Chief Judge herself, then clear the game relatively smoothly, thus escaping judgment? Rather than needing to participate completely passively like now, risking being voted to death in the end?"
Cao Haichuan shook his head, "No, that’s not the reason.
"If Chen Yumei became the Chief Judge herself and cleared the game smoothly, it would obviously create contradictions in the game mechanism.
"The prerequisite for becoming Chief Judge is giving relatively extreme answers in the five questions before the game starts.
"But if this kind of person serves as Chief Judge, they would most likely be unable to pass this judgment. If they passed the judgment very smoothly, that would instead increase other players’ suspicion that she’s the God’s Imitator.
"Whether Chen Yumei lied during the lie detection or didn’t lie, afterwards other players could potentially find out by purchasing the game records. This wouldn’t be secure.
"If she really were the God’s Imitator, she shouldn’t be unable to think this through.
"Hypothetically, if a God’s Imitator really designed a game to judge themselves, the optimal solution definitely wouldn’t be to obtain an advantageous identity.
"It would be best to let someone else become the advantageous identity, choose a disadvantageous identity for themselves, then find a way to slip through."
Fu Chen was stunned, "But isn’t that exactly what Chen Yumei did in this game?"Cao Haichuan shook his head, "It looks like it, but actually it isn’t.
"The problem lies in the initial screening mechanism.
"If Chen Yumei were the God’s Imitator, she could have completely adopted more covert methods to screen others out and hide herself well.
"She shouldn’t have used this lie-detection question-and-answer format."
Everyone nodded, roughly understanding.
Chen Yumei indeed seemed more like the God’s Imitator than Li Jiang, but if she really were the God’s Imitator, everyone might very likely not suspect her at all.
She could have used other methods to make Jiang He become the Chief Judge, such as creating a small mechanism similar to Farmer’s Walk, then giving different weights based on gender.
When choosing her assistant, she also could have not chosen Li Jiang, but chosen another player with weaker physical strength.
That way, Jiang He, as someone with relatively superior physical strength among women, would most likely be chosen as Chief Judge, and the game would ultimately still proceed to the same ending.
Without those initial five questions, and with Chen Yumei paddling the entire time without giving any opinions, how could others guess her true inner thoughts?
Even if they purchased her game records, they couldn’t see any flaws at all.
In that case, it could almost be called a perfect crime as a God’s Imitator.
Even if someone suspected Chen Yumei was the God’s Imitator, they fundamentally couldn’t find any evidence.
Therefore, Lin Sizhi and Cao Haichuan, based on this point, believed Chen Yumei was not the God’s Imitator.
Lin Sizhi added, "Of course, we’ve preset a premise that ’Chen Yumei didn’t suddenly have an intelligence drop’, so we can’t completely rule out her suspicion.
"But regardless, God’s Imitators capable of creating these games must definitely not be stupid, and must definitely have thought things through carefully. They shouldn’t leave such self-contradictory loopholes."
Wang Yongxin let out a long breath, "So the conclusion is:
"The God’s Imitator of ’Childbirth Judgment’ is neither the God’s Imitator of ’King’s Judgment’, nor Li Jiang or Chen Yumei.
"And of course it’s even more impossible to be Jiang He, Yang Yuting, or other judged people in this game.
"Because those other judged criminals were basically in a state with no human rights. If they really encountered a Chief Judge with a rather one-track mind who just killed them all, the God’s Imitator couldn’t possibly take that risk.
"We reasoned for so long, and the conclusion is: this God’s Imitator never entered the game they designed at all.
"So we worked for nothing."
Li Renshu reminded, "It’s not really working for nothing. At least it’s very helpful for understanding God’s Imitators’ thinking.
"Haven’t you noticed? Although the New World basically hasn’t revealed any more rules about God’s Imitators to us, we’ve figured out a lot ourselves.
"For example:
"God’s Imitators don’t necessarily have to enter their own games, so not every game can end by rooting out the God’s Imitator. Finding the God’s Imitator is more like some kind of hidden clearance secret. Not every game will have one.
"For the purpose of hiding themselves, God’s Imitators most likely won’t keep designing overly homogeneous games. They might even deliberately make some games with styles vastly different from their original style. We can’t determine God’s Imitators solely through game style.
"To find God’s Imitators, the most important thing is analyzing their ’purpose’ and ’intent’, but each God’s Imitator’s situation is different. We can’t mechanically apply one approach.
"With these clues, finding God’s Imitators at least won’t be like looking for a needle in a haystack as before. There’s at least some hope now."
She looked at everyone, "Alright, today’s review has gone on a bit too long. Let’s stop here.
"Everyone worked hard. Get some rest early."
...
That evening, Wang Yongxin and Yang Yuting came to the small room on the third floor.
"Is your injury okay?" Wang Yongxin asked.
Yang Yuting looked at her bandaged wound, "It’s okay, just a bit itchy. Dr. Zheng said there’s nothing serious, just rest well."
Both of them fell into brief silence.
Obviously, this judgment game and Jiang He’s death counted as a black swan event for the two of them, full of surprises.
From a negative perspective, Wang Yongxin had one less person he could potentially recruit, and the position of Li Renshu’s five-person group in this community became even more solid.
The death of a member could have originally become an opportunity that would lead to community division.
If the death immunity token had been used improperly, it could very likely have caused the originally stable structure in the community to change again but Li Renshu handled this incident very calmly, and instead won quite a bit of goodwill.
Of course, were all people satisfied with Li Renshu’s performance this time?
Would anyone feel that Li Renshu not saving Jiang He used overly subjective standards?
Hard to say, after all, people’s hearts are hard to read but generally speaking, even if this degree of suspicion really existed, it couldn’t possibly be revealed in the short term.
However, from a positive perspective, Jiang He’s death also removed a mine from Wang Yongxin’s already fragile small group.
Wang Yongxin didn’t dwell too much on it and said, "Let’s let the past be past. Discussing those things further is meaningless.
"I think the main issue we two need to consider now is what kind of female player the community should recruit next.
"Although theoretically speaking, this matter will most likely still be decided by everyone’s vote, and Li Renshu might guide the discussion, your opinion should also carry sufficient weight.
"On one hand, regarding what kind of female player to specifically recruit, the opinions of other female players in the community will carry great weight. You and Xu Tong can bind two votes, which can influence others to some extent.
"On the other hand, you are after all the direct victim of this incident. As long as your opinion sounds relatively reasonable, most swing votes will stand on your side out of sympathy or consideration."
Yang Yuting thought carefully for a moment, "Do you think... finding another actuary is possible? Luo Wei’s situation was an accident after all. Not every actuary can be like her, right?"
Wang Yongxin silently shook his head, "That won’t work too well.
"From a rational standpoint, Luo Wei’s betrayal was a low-probability event. Recruiting another actuary most likely won’t result in a similar situation. But from an emotional standpoint, most people in the community already have certain prejudices against this profession. Proposing this plan again has a very low possibility of passing.
"Even if we want to choose a high-intelligence woman, we must change to another profession."

chapters.title: Chapter 199: Time Intervals
chapters.content:
Yang Yuting thought carefully for a moment, "In that case, I do have an idea.
"A female mechanical engineer or engineer, what do you think?"
Wang Yongxin thought for a moment, "I do tend toward female players with science and engineering backgrounds. Other people in the community should be the same.
"Currently our community has too many liberal arts professions. Recruiting a pure science and engineering profession might be a good choice.
"I’ve also considered professions like architect before.
"What’s your reason for considering mechanical engineer or engineer?"
Yang Yuting sighed quietly, "Two considerations, I suppose.
"On one hand, I think female players in these professions are indeed more reliable, relatively pragmatic, with a lower possibility of situations like Luo Wei’s and Jiang He’s occurring.
"On the other hand, it’s also to continue supplementing our community’s current knowledge structure.
"From ’King’s Judgment’ to ’Childbirth Judgment’, many games have started featuring more and more mechanisms."Thinking about it, we made a very basic mistake in ’Childbirth Judgment’ before. We completely didn’t think that those mechanisms could be reused.
"Of course, from the post-game review, this was indeed a rather stupid error, also caused by the gender and mechanism mismatch, but regardless, not noticing is not noticing.
"If it were a profession more familiar with machinery, they might be able to think of this point more easily.
"Moreover, if it’s a similar profession, although she’s female, her physical fitness would most likely be more advantageous than average women, right?
"From what we can see now, there’s a probability of physical strength-related game segments appearing.
"A female player with better physical strength, although still can’t compare to male players, but if the mechanism is designed according to female player physical strength standards, can still easily open up a gap from average female players."
Wang Yongxin considered for a moment, then nodded, "Well, if we propose a female mechanical engineer or engineer, it should most likely pass.
"After all, people can only learn lessons from the most recent history.
"Our community’s recruitment is the same. Everyone will subconsciously correct errors from the last game, and can’t really look very far ahead."
Yang Yuting was stunned, "Hm? People can only learn lessons from the most recent history? What do you mean?"
Wang Yongxin explained, "Oh, this is a concept from history.
"Simply put, after each unified dynasty is established, although they generally continue the previous dynasty’s systems, they also make some systemic corrections.
"But this kind of correction can often only target the previous dynasty’s problems. Sometimes it triggers some new problems.
"For example, the ’historical cycle phenomenon’ appears.
"Dynasty A makes a certain mistake leading to its downfall. Dynasty B learns this lesson and makes changes, then falls due to another lesson. Dynasty C learns Dynasty B’s lesson but returns to Dynasty A’s old path, falling for the same reason as Dynasty A...
"So there’s also a saying: ’The only lesson humanity learns from history is that it has never truly learned any lessons.’
"But there’s no helping it, because the future is still too vague and ethereal. Rather than overly caring about the future or the too-distant past, it’s better to only focus on the not-too-distant past."
Wang Yongxin paused slightly, then continued, "Besides this, recruiting this kind of person has another issue, which is... her ideology may not necessarily be closer to ours.
"If this new member recognizes Li Renshu or Cai Zhiyuan more, that would be a bit awkward.
"I need to think ahead about how to build goodwill in front of this new member, trying to get her to stand on our side more."
Yang Yuting sighed quietly, "If that situation really occurs, there’s no helping it.
"My first requirement for recruitment now is a reliable and stable teammate. As for which side she specifically stands on, I don’t care anymore."
Wang Yongxin couldn’t say much, just consoled, "Well, I understand."
Obviously, this judgment game had frightened Yang Yuting considerably, to the point that currently for her, safety and stability trumped everything, with quite a tendency to want to give up this small group and completely place her fate in Li Renshu’s hands.
Wang Yongxin initially established this small group to better protect himself, to prevent being subjected to "tyranny of the majority" through voting but as time passed, Li Renshu was recognized by more and more players in the community, and these external small groups naturally gradually collapsed.
Although Wang Yongxin was somewhat worried, he could only accept and understand this.
After all, when he had just come out of ’King’s Judgment’, he also had some PTSD tendencies. The desire for safety overwhelmed everything.
...
Three days later, morning.
Everyone had already finished breakfast, but still gathered in the hall. Some read books, while others were simply waiting.
Actually, yesterday morning some people were waiting, but after waiting and waiting, no new recruitment notice appeared on the large screen.
Obvious anxiety appeared on many people’s faces.
Fortunately, after waiting a while, the recruitment notice finally came.
[This community has a player vacancy. In 96 hours, the community will admit a new player for supplementation, becoming the new Player No. 2.]
Seeing this sentence, the heavy stone in many people’s hearts fell, but it also pressed down on their hearts.
Li Renshu’s expression was very serious, "As expected, the time interval for each community recruitment keeps increasing.
"The first recruitment notice appeared the second day after the game ended. The second was on the third day after the game ended. This time is already the fourth day after the game ended.
"Not only that, the time for the new player to arrive at the community has also changed from the initial 24 hours to 48 hours, and now to 96 hours.
"Looking at the intervals between most game starts... before the next game begins, our community probably won’t be able to gather 12 people."
Cai Zhiyuan had previously discussed this speculation with Lin Sizhi, and it seemed they guessed correctly.
The community couldn’t frequently recruit. Each interval kept getting longer.
Community 17’s player deaths were far below the average death count of other communities, yet there was still a personnel vacancy. Other communities with more weak players were even more so.
Li Renshu was also somewhat disappointed, but her emotions were relatively stable. She looked at everyone, "According to our previously established principle, the community’s male-female ratio should still be maintained at 6:6, so this time we also need to recruit a female player.
"Regarding the new member’s profession, does anyone have any thoughts?"
Wang Yongxin looked at Yang Yuting. They had already discussed this question but before Yang Yuting could speak, Cai Zhiyuan spoke first, "Regarding recruitment, I have some different views. Can we chat about them first?"
Everyone was somewhat surprised, but similar discussions had always been open for everyone to speak freely, so most people expressed tacit consent.
Cai Zhiyuan pointed at the large screen, "No matter what kind of player we decide to recruit now, it will take 96 hours for them to arrive, which means it will definitely be after the next game.
"So there’s no rush with this matter.
"I even think we no longer need to use this method to recruit."

chapters.title: Chapter 200: Recruitment or Poaching
chapters.content:
Even Li Renshu was slightly surprised. Obviously, before saying these words, Cai Zhiyuan hadn’t communicated with her privately in advance.
Cai Zhiyuan explained, "First, I believe that on this kind of issue, group discussion may not necessarily produce the most correct result.
"From the two recruitments so far, recruiting Dr. Zheng was a good result, but recruiting Luo Wei was a thorough mistake.
"This mistake doesn’t just refer to Luo Wei’s betrayal.
"Everyone should remember that in the last game, we encountered three reproduction-related questions.
"Let’s hypothesize. If Luo Wei hadn’t betrayed us but chose to stay, then in the last game, might there have been a possibility of getting all the questions wrong?
"Because apart from Aunt Zhou, no one in our community could answer these three questions.
"This is enough to prove the importance of ’maintaining community diversity’ that Renshu has always emphasized, and the unreliability of having all community members vote on selecting people.
"It was precisely Renshu’s proposal at that time to recruit an older member with a common profession that was the correct choice.
"If we had recruited an older farmer, worker, or teacher at that time, she most likely could have answered these questions just as easily as Aunt Zhou."Everyone fell into brief silence.
If things were as Cai Zhiyuan said, and Luo Wei hadn’t betrayed them, then ’Childbirth Judgment’ indeed might very likely have had an even more disastrous outcome.
These three questions in ’Childbirth Judgment’ did seem quite lenient, with two opportunities to ask the audience, and even if the audience answered incorrectly, they could eliminate wrong answers but the first two questions only seemed like gimmes because of Zhou Guifen’s existence.
If Zhou Guifen hadn’t joined Community 17 and had been replaced with Luo Wei, then Luo Wei would certainly also 100% not know the answers to these two questions.
What about Community 13? Probably hard to say as well.
If both communities answered incorrectly, even after eliminating two wrong answers, the players in the field would still have to choose one from the other two wrong answers.
If they chose wrong again, that would be completely over. The game would be completely unplayable.
This round of questions could even be said to show mercy from the God’s Imitator who designed this game. What if next time, the game only allowed one side’s audience to answer? Or what if answering incorrectly didn’t eliminate wrong answers?
That could very likely cause catastrophic consequences.
Of course, Cai Zhiyuan’s statement at this moment had somewhat of a suspicion of elevating matters to a political level and using the topic to make a point.
After all, when recruiting Luo Wei, no one could predict that a reproduction-related judgment game would appear at this time but from the result, recruiting Luo Wei was indeed a mistake.
Li Renshu had proposed recruiting an older member with a common profession at that time, such as a worker, farmer, or teacher. If they had recruited according to this requirement, there very likely wouldn’t have been a betrayal, and she could have perfectly answered the questions in ’Childbirth Judgment’ just like Zhou Guifen.
Li Renshu hadn’t insisted on this point at the time, but ultimately chose to have everyone vote.
So naturally, this mistake should be borne by everyone.
Li Renshu looked at Cai Zhiyuan. She herself also felt very surprised.
Because before the second recruitment, Li Renshu had chatted privately with Cai Zhiyuan, and Cai Zhiyuan was also opposed to recruiting a common profession at that time but now he clearly stood on her side.
Hard to say how much of Cai Zhiyuan’s words were sincere.
However, for Li Renshu, there was absolutely no reason to undermine him at this moment, because Cai Zhiyuan’s words were actually enhancing her prestige.
So she could only listen silently.
Cai Zhiyuan continued, "I believe this problem is not accidental.
"Because as long as it’s multi-person voting, no matter how much we emphasize supplementing knowledge structures, everyone will still subconsciously choose new members they personally prefer.
"In other words, the new members chosen by community voting are not the optimal solution at all, but rather the result of the optimal solution being adjusted toward the preferences of most members in our community.
"This result could very likely be a case of a slight error leading to a huge deviation."
Everyone fell silent again.
What Cai Zhiyuan said had some merit. Although everyone knew the importance of ’maintaining diversity’, this wasn’t something so easy to accomplish.
When most people voted, they would still mix in their own subjective preferences, possibly even unconsciously.
Wang Yongxin heard the implication in Cai Zhiyuan’s words and frowned slightly, "So you mean that all future recruitments should be decided by Li Renshu alone?"
Cai Zhiyuan shook his head, "Of course not.
"What I mean is that completely arbitrary voting, or completely handing this power to one person, are both inappropriate.
"There are always some people who see further ahead. Their opinions need some additional weight.
"Of course, this is just a kind of proposal. Whether to continue trying to push forward still needs careful consideration.
"Back to this recruitment topic, I believe that rather than continuing to select people for recruitment, we might as well try to poach people from games.
"The advantage of self-recruitment is that we can customize the age and profession of new members to a certain degree.
"But from previous situations, the Gallery’s selection isn’t very reliable.
"Moreover, players who just entered the New World very likely don’t have a clear understanding of themselves or this world, and their personalities are completely uncontrollable.
"But if they’re players who have already survived in the New World for a period of time, there shouldn’t be too serious problems in this regard.
"Because up to now, the Gallery has already eliminated many unreliable players for us. Those who are stubborn, obstinate, or don’t understand teamwork, most can’t survive until now.
"The remaining players, relatively speaking, should have a relatively clear understanding of themselves and the community.
"They won’t have situations like Luo Wei’s.
"If we poach people, although we can’t customize the new member’s profession, we can observe their behavior in games and consider whether they’re compatible with our community, which is actually a more reliable choice.
"For example, a new member like Aunt Zhou is very perfect for our community.
"We don’t need someone very clever or with independent leadership ability. As long as they’re stable, reliable, able to execute team decisions, and able to supplement our knowledge system, that’s enough."
Hearing this, quite a few people were nodding.
Cai Zhiyuan’s conclusion was indeed somewhat arbitrary. Who could assert that players poached from other communities in games would definitely be more reliable than new members?
But most people reviewed their previous experiences and indeed could be easily persuaded by this viewpoint.
After all, as Wang Yongxin had said to Yang Yuting before: people are creatures of experience, and can only learn lessons from recent history.
Wang Yongxin frowned slightly, "But this brings up a new problem:
"If it’s a game with very few people, we most likely won’t encounter suitable candidates. If it’s a game with many people, who specifically should we poach, and who decides?"

chapters.title: Chapter 202: The Only Candidate
chapters.content:
Hearing these words, the originally somewhat tense atmosphere relaxed considerably.
"Hm? That makes sense. It’s time to make Lawyer Lin do more work!"
"I have no objection if it’s given to Lawyer Lin. Even if he decides to bring in Lu Xinyi, I’d support it."
"Pfft, wishful thinking. Taking everything, huh? Lu Xinyi is ruling like an emperor in Community 3. Why would she come here?"
"I was just giving an example."
Wang Yongxin also nodded, "Well, if that’s the case, I’d only accept Lawyer Lin having this recruitment power."
He looked at Lin Sizhi, "This time you have no reason to decline.
"If you don’t take this job, it means you think this method is unreliable.
"We might as well honestly return to the old path of voting for recruitment. Even if we recruit wrongly, it doesn’t matter. Since it’s a group decision, no matter what consequences arise, everyone shares the responsibility."
Cai Zhiyuan also looked at Lin Sizhi but after brief consideration, Lin Sizhi readily agreed, "Sure, no problem."Now it was Cai Zhiyuan’s turn to be surprised.
Because previously, whether it was proposals or the death immunity token, Lin Sizhi had directly declined everything cleanly, so Cai Zhiyuan subconsciously thought this time would be the same.
From the current situation, only very few players could obtain the ’recruitment power’ in games.
Everyone had to recognize that this player simultaneously possessed the ability to judge other players in ’loyalty, values, and personal ability’ before giving this power.
To judge others, you first have to meet these standards yourself, right?
So this was actually having all players select someone based on these three conditions.
Wang Yongxin would definitely be excluded, because many players in the community didn’t quite recognize his values and somewhat doubted his loyalty.
Among the remaining people, as long as Lin Sizhi didn’t take this job, this position would still most likely fall to Li Renshu.
In that case, Cai Zhiyuan’s goal would naturally be perfectly achieved.
Unexpectedly, Lin Sizhi accepted very straightforwardly, making this issue suddenly no longer in suspense.
After brief consideration, Cai Zhiyuan nodded, "That’s naturally best."
Wang Yongxin had been somewhat nervous before, but now felt like laughing.
Although Lin Sizhi had been viewed as a member of the five-person group from beginning to end, he had actually never truly integrated, nor did it mean he would forever sit by and watch the situation develop in a direction favorable to the current power core.
For most players in the community at this time, although they had recognized Li Renshu as the power core, it didn’t mean they were willing to hand all power to Li Renshu.
The power to submit proposals was given, the power over the death immunity token was given. If the recruitment power was given too, it would be a bit much.
So as long as Lin Sizhi was willing to accept, other people would definitely give him the recruitment power.
Although Wang Yongxin himself couldn’t obtain this power, the current situation was a completely acceptable result.
Li Renshu had no objection to this either.
"Good, then the power to ’poach people’ is entrusted to Lawyer Lin.
"Other players who enter games with Lawyer Lin can also have veto power. The specific situation will be decided by you all in the game.
"Do we need to pass a special proposal for this?"
Wang Yongxin thought for a moment, "Let’s pass it. Even if only for the sense of ceremony, it’s necessary."
Others unanimously agreed.
Obviously, if this matter wasn’t determined through a proposal, other players would still have the possibility to exploit loopholes.
